News.title: Newcastle and Liverpool serve up thrilling tribute to Kevin Keegan
News.content:
It is fitting that Newcastle United vs Liverpool is a Premier League opening weekend fixture following the death of Kevin Keegan at the age of 75 last month.

All corners of St James’ Park will pay tribute and show their appreciation for the former player and manager who means a great deal to both sets of supporters.

Fans will find a printed message from the Keegan family on the back of black and white cards on their seat, which they will hold up to display a mural before kick-off.

As well as playing for both clubs, Keegan was Newcastle’s manager when they were beaten by a last-gasp Stan Collymore goal at Anfield in April 1996, a 4-3 defeat remembered as one of the great Premier League games.

This fixture usually delivers entertainment, and with new managers Matthias Jaissle and Andoni Iraola promising front-footed, ‘vertical’ football, there should be goals. That was certainly the case last August, when Newcastle fought back from two down with 10 men, before Rio Ngumoha scored a memorable winner.

It has been a summer of tumult for Newcastle, losing manager Eddie Howe, as well as key players Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes. There has been bullish talk of “Newcastle 2.0” from David Hopkinson, the club’s chief executive, and the club believe they have found a promising coach, but fans have understandably revised expectations downwards.

Liverpool are a difficult team to read; champions only 18 months ago but brittle last season, which resulted in Arne Slot’s dismissal. Iraola’s appointment is a shift back towards Jurgen Klopp’s style. That will be music to the ears of Anfield regulars, but holes remain in the squad. Central midfield has not been replenished; they need a Mohamed Salah replacement, and their strength at full-back is questionable. Much will depend on how 21-year-old central defender Jérémy Jacquet fares alongside Vigin van Dijk but he impressed in pre-season.



Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Frustrated Russell fails to make up ground as Norris wins incident-packed Dutch GP
News.content:
George Russell had another frustrating Sunday as the Dutch Grand Prix weekend slipped by with him failing to reduce his deficit to leader Kimi Antonelli. In a thrilling finale to the 72-lap race at the Dutch seaside, Lando Norris took his second victory in a row with two bold overtakes in one lap.

Yet compatriot Russell was irritated by Mercedes team orders for him to let Antonelli through into second place in the closing stages. It was a decision he believed risked a double podium for the team and threatened to put him even further behind his team-mate in the standings, with two charging Ferraris close behind. It was a race that, once again, fell away, despite Russell doing little wrong.

“Is he [Antonelli] fighting for the win or is he planning to catch Norris?” he asked, when the McLaren driver was 11 seconds down the road – the margin he would win by. “Yeah – we just lost a double podium here, mate,” was his response after moving aside.

Whilst Norris, who lost his lead from pole to Antonelli on the first lap, sealed the victory with two superb overtakes on lap 54 – first the Italian and then Lewis Hamilton – Russell had to mount a stout defence from Hamilton to secure third. It was against the odds, as both Ferraris, like Antonelli, were on fresh rubber after pitting under a late virtual safety car. Like Russell, Hamilton was critical of his team for their strategy choices.

Russell’s first podium finish since Silverstone – with his sprint victory on Saturday – means he at least retakes second place in the championship from Hamilton, but trails Antonelli by the same 59 point-gap he had after Hungary. That is despite him looking the faster and more comfortable Mercedes driver on Friday and Saturday.

News.title: Enzo Maresca tinkers his way to nervy Man City win
News.content:
Few in elite sport have the luxury of managing their own endings as Pep Guardiola did at Manchester City, yet no one can ever fully control a beginning. Enzo Maresca’s City started their Premier League season with a win, in the end, but three points masked the scale of the job he faces.

The narrative focus has been the impossibility of filling the personality void Guardiola leaves at a club sculpted in his image. That macro reading overlooks the number of distinct issues with City that Maresca must fix. A new midfield has to be recruited then blooded, a jittery defence needs settling down, and Phil Foden clearly requires help to recover the form which made him Premier League player of the year as recently as 2024.

All of that can wait after this victory against Bournemouth, which quietened some of the alarms from last weekend’s 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in Cardiff. Josko Gvardiol scored an injury-time winner after City had trailed for most of the match, much of it a sloppy slog for the home side, who went behind in the 26th minute. The introduction of Rayan Cherki for Nico O’Reilly revived some familiar attacking effusiveness.

A lesser-spotted VAR-aided double celebration capped a tense but ultimately joyful day for Maresca. Marc Guéhi equalised from Cherki’s well-taken corner in the final minutes, then the expanded Etihad Stadium rapturously celebrated Gvardiol’s apparent winner, only to see it flagged offside. Video assistant Paul Howard intervened to show Gvardiol was onside from Cherki’s pass, before City’s fans, players and staff shouted twice as loud for twice as long to salute a morale-boosting victory.

News.title: How to spend a weekend in Lake Garda
News.content:
Lake Garda’s glittering wind-swept waters have long attracted poets, artists, writers and politicians, from DH Lawrence to Wolfgang Goethe – not least Mussolini, who ran the Italian Socialist Republic from the lakefront town of Salò on the western shore.

Fringed by the Dolomites to the north, Italy’s largest lake is Mediterranean both in feel and in flavour, with a mild, temperate climate and a decidedly slow pace of life. Hills are carpeted in olive trees and vineyards, while citrus groves are thick with plump, juicy lemons. In lakefront villages, restaurant tables spill out onto pretty waterfront squares, while boats zip across glimmering waters.

The lower basin is punctuated with sandy coves and gentle rolling hills, while travelling north, the lake takes on a new appearance, with hills replaced by sheer jagged cliffs that plunge into the waters. The northern shore is swept by mountain winds that create the perfect conditions for watersports, with windsailing, kitesurfing, and flyboarding making this a premier destination for outdoor enthusiasts.

News.title: How to spend a perfect weekend in Lake Como
News.content:
An hour drive north of Milan, Lake Como is the most glamorous of Italy’s lakes, hemmed in by the snow-capped Alps with picture-perfect villages on the water. Milanesi pop here for the day for a breath of fresh air and to soak up the fabulous vistas, while international visitors – the Clooneys, the Kennedys – have long been drawn by the grand lakefront hotels and the elegant mahogany Riva boats that zip along the lake’s deep blue waters.

Smart hotels and expensive boats aside, Lake Como is rich in culture, with opulent villas that once belonged to artists, writers, opera singers and explorers. Pliny the Elder, author of the first encyclopaedia, was born here, while 19th-century soprano Giuditta Pasta is known to have entertained composers Bellini and Donizetti in her lakefront residence on the eastern shore.

Though famous spots such as pretty Bellagio still pull in the majority of visitors, the lake has retained its authenticity, with plenty of sleepy fishing villages, such as Laglio, Torno and Nesso, home to rustic, family-run trattorias serving up traditional hearty fare, including risotto al pesce persico (risotto with perch).

News.title: Erling Haaland cuts off his trademark blond hair
News.content:
It is a new-look City in more ways than one this term with head coach Enzo Maresca looking to kickstart a new era following Pep Guardiola’s exit.

Maresca is hoping for an immediate return to form in City’s Premier League opener after a chastening 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in the Community Shield last week.

So far, only Elliot Anderson has arrived but Maresca is hopeful the club will be active in the transfer market. Rodri has left for Barcelona while Savinho is closing in on a move to Tottenham.

“I’ll try to find a new Rodri – it is what it is,” the former Chelsea manager said. “Rodri, before he arrived here, he didn’t win the Ballon d’Or, he didn’t win the Champions League, he didn’t win the Club World Cup. Then he joined the club and then after he achieved many important things. Now the target for us is to try to find the new Rodri.

“When David Silva was here, everyone was worried - Kevin [De Bruyne] arrived. When Sergio Agüero was here, everyone was worried – Erling [Haaland] arrived. When Ferdinando left, Rodri arrived. It’s just about this.

“When they leave, you need to be good and recruit the next one. They are all similar – David, Kevin, Fernandinho, Rodri, Agüero, Erling. It’s just normal, it’s a change. It’s not a problem, just go again and try to do the right things.”

Sports.title: Liam Delap ‘closes in on shock Premier League transfer’ with Chelsea nightmare set to come to an end
Sports.content:
LIAM DELAP is reportedly close to ending his nightmare spell at Chelsea.

The striker failed to impress after a £30m move from Ipswich, scoring just one Premier League goal last term.

But Delap is now close to a £40m move to Nottingham Forest, which would see Chelsea make a profit on what had, until now, been a disastrous investment.



Oliver Glasner has taken over as Forest manager, becoming one of the highest-paid Premier League bosses.



And after frequently rowing with the Crystal Palace hierarchy over their lack of ambition in the transfer market, the Austrian will likely be expecting the full backing of exuberant Forest owner Evangelos Marinakis.

The East Midlanders drew a blank in a dismal 1-0 loss at home to Leeds on opening day, with neither starter Igor Jesus or the veteran Chris Wood able to hit the back of the net.

And with Taiwo Awoniyi having completed a £9m move to newly-promoted Coventry, Forest appear to have identified Delap as the man to add some firepower.



After netting an impressive 12 goals for Kieran McKenna’s Ipswich two seasons ago, Delap appeared to forget where the goal is altogether after his move to Stamford Bridge.

His only strike came in a 2-1 defeat at neighbours Fulham in January, with his spell at the Blues so unsuccessful that fans started to pine for the sometimes brilliant, sometimes infuriating Nicolas Jackson, who was loaned out to Bayern Munich.

SunSport understands that Delap could become a Nottingham Forest player as soon as this weekend.

Chelsea have already broadened their options in the number nine position, with Danny Welbeck brought in to provide competition for Joao Pedro.



Emmanuel Emegha has also completed his scheduled move from Strasbourg, with it remaining to be seen how, and if, new boss Xabi Alonso will use him.

And Jackson is back with the Blues, but believed to be a target for Aston Villa.

Sports.title: Richard Keys replaced by glamorous London 2012 Olympic medallist as new face of beIN Sports after 13 years
Sports.content:
KAYLYN KYLE is the new face of football at beIN Sports – after replacing Richard Keys.

The former midfielder, 37, featured for the Rest of the World at Soccer Aid in June.



And Kyle announced her abrupt exit from Apple TV’s coverage of Major League Soccer in an emotional statement earlier this month.

The Canadian is now preparing for a new life in Qatar after being confirmed as beIN Sport’s new lead presenter.



The Athletic report Kyle is set to be confirmed as Keys’ successor ahead of being on hosting duties for Nottingham Forest’s trip to Liverpool on Saturday.

She is also on course to be front and centre for Champions League showdowns.

Qatar-based beIN Sports grabbed the broadcasting rights across the Middle East and North Africa for Europe’s elite tournament and the Premier League.

Kyle won 101 international caps for Canada and bagged bronze at the London 2012 Olympics.



Spells were also enjoyed with the likes of Vancouver Whitecaps, Seattle Reign, Boston Breakers, Houston Dash, Portland Thorns and Orlando Pride during her stunning career.

Since announcing her retirement in 2017, Kyle has been making waves as a popular broadcaster.

SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Canadian TV company TSN handed Kyle her first on-screen role in 2017 before she later had a spell as a sideline reporter for Inter Miami.



The glamorous presenter also covered MLS clashes on Apple TV for four years and worked for beIN Sports as Lionel Messi spearheaded Argentina to glory at the 2022 World Cup.

Kyle has seen her number of Instagram followers surge to 152,000 after giving fans a glimpse of her lavish lifestyle away from the pitch.

She is married to Harrison Heath, who is the son of Everton icon Adrian Heath.



Keys, 69, and Andy Gray walked away from beIN Sports at the end of last season.

It ended their 13-year stint with the broadcasting giant, having joined following their sacking by Sky Sports, and they have since launched a new podcast together.

Sports.title: How Arsenal’s new ‘ghost’ set piece trick baffled Coventry to seal perfect start to Premier League title defence
Sports.content:
ARSENAL kicked off the defence of their Premier League title with a convincing 3-0 win over Coventry on Friday night.

While the likes of Manchester United, Manchester City and Liverpool all struggled in their opening games, there was no such trouble for the Gunners.



Goals from Kai Havertz, Bukayo Saka and Martin Odegaard swept Frank Lampard’s newly-promoted side away.

However, set-piece mastermind Nicolas Jover also delivered once again – by unveiling a brand new ‘ghost’ corner routine that completely baffled the visitors.



SunSport’s tactical expert Dean Scoggins broke down the victory for Mikel Arteta’s side in the latest episode of Tactics Exposed.

First things first, did you spot the little ghost trick?



Look at Ben White’s run on the blind side of the goalkeeper where nobody’s going to pick him up because Coventry are marking zonally – and so he’s not been seen.

Arsenal take a sneaky short corner, after the one-two he receives the ball from Bukayo Saka and he gets on the ball inside the area.

Riccardo Calafiori does a job as the decoy man as Arsenal crash the box and then White passes to Tzolis.

Arsenal taking even their set-piece tactics to another level.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

We’ve got to acknowledge that with the refereeing this year and all the talk of the cut down in grappling, Arsenal need to find another way to be a threat at set pieces and on matchday one, boy did they do it.

And while it was the old guard on the scoresheet, it was new boy Christos Tzolis who stole the show.

In a lesson in Greek philosophy, the wide man proved he understands exactly what Mikel Arteta wants from him, disrupting Coventry’s defence by running across the line into the areas his manager wants him – not just standing there and making himself easy to mark.

That also opened space for Riccardo Calafiori down the left for Arsenal.



At other times, he unselfishly kept the width and that led to the Saka goal, as he stayed out of the congestion centrally to put the low ball across.

It was a really impressive start from Tzolis, knowing when to come in and when to go out – the Tzolis Hokey-Cokey.



He may not be an elite winger like Vinicius but he is showing an elite tactical brain straight away.

Finally, Arsenal also debuted a daring new-look 3-1-6 formation in possession, using Myles Lewis-Skelly to dominate central areas – and the gaffer may have taken inspiration from Paris Saint-Germain.



The elite young midfielder rotated effortlessly with Declan Rice in the middle of the three and the solo one in midfield to enable Arsenal to overload the Coventry defence with six attacking players.

There were times last year when Arsenal got a bit stodgy and didn’t take enough risks but with Lewis-Skelly in the Marco Verratti role, it would be ridiculous to sell him.



The 3-1-6 gives six men in attack with the full-backs released due to the midfielder dropping in.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

They created a 4v4, a 3 or 4v4 and an overload on the two pressers. That shape gives them more players in the right positions.

Ben White even hit long cross-field passes because of the overload which means even if they did lose the ball, they can counter-press 2v1.

Sports.title: Man City ‘ready to hijack Tottenham’s Cody Gakpo transfer’ as Enzo Maresca’s men ‘begin talks’ for Liverpool star
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER CITY have reportedly made a shock move to beat Tottenham to the signing of Liverpool winger Cody Gakpo.

The Sky Blues got their Premier League season off to a winning start as they came from behind to beat Bournemouth yesterday.



But City boss Enzo Maresca, who was appointed as Pep Guardiola’s successor during the summer, is in the market for more attacking reinforcements.

And the Sky Blues are threatening to hijack Tottenham’s move for Gakpo, 27, in the final days of the transfer window.



Fabrizio Romano reports City have begun talks with the Dutchman’s camp over a surprise switch to the Etihad Stadium.

But Tottenham are still in active discussions with Gakpo and personal terms have already been agreed.

The former PSV Eindhoven talisman found the net in Liverpool’s last-gasp draw with Newcastle yesterday.

Gakpo was named in the Merseyside giants’ starting line-up despite ongoing uncertainty over his future.

And Liverpool chief Andoni Iraola, who replaced Arne Slot in the dugout in June, wants to fend off bids unless he can bring in another winger.

But City are hoping to lure Gakpo away from Anfield before the transfer window slams shut.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Maresca’s latest target got his name on the scoresheet seven times in the Premier League last season.

And Gakpo played a key role in the Netherlands reaching the last-32 at the World Cup before their penalty shootout heartbreak against Morocco.

He bagged a brace in a 5-1 thumping of Graham Potter’s Sweden in the group stage.

Gakpo also notched a goal in the showdown with Morocco – which came days after his partner Noa van der Bij’s heartbreaking miscarriage announcement.



City shattered their transfer record to land Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest last month.

Lille midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi is on course to become the Sky Blues’ latest big-money arrival.

Sports.title: Newcastle ‘agree £50m Nico Gonzalez transfer as Man City star gives green light to joining Matthias Jaissle’s side’
Sports.content:
NEWCASTLE have reportedly reached a verbal agreement over the £50million transfer for Nico Gonzalez.

Gonzalez, 24, joined Manchester City in January 2025 from Porto but has struggled to cement himself as a regular in the first team.



Now he seems surplus to requirements at the Etihad – and up for sale.

And St James’ Park looks set to be his next destination.



Newcastle will now offer him the platform to impress in the Premier League.

The Magpies have been desperate to land a new central midfielder this summer following the sales of Bruno Guimaraes and Sandro Tonali.

The pair left for Arsenal and Tottenham for £75m and £100m respectively.

That saw the Toon needing to bolster the engine room.

Matthias Jaissle started 18-year-old debutant Sean Steur and Lewis Miley, 20, as his midfield pair for the dramatic 2-2 draw with Liverpool on Sunday.

But he seems to have finally landed a big-name signing.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

According to Fabrizio Romano, the clubs have agreed a £50m fee for the midfielder.

It is understood the Magpies will pay a fixed fee of £47m with a further £3m in add-ons.

Gonzalez has been given the green light to travel to Newcastle ahead of sealing the deal.

The former Barcelona prospect has played 54 times for the Cityzens and scored four goals.



The most important of those was the winner in April’s FA Cup semi-final against Southampton.

Gonzalez was an unused sub for Sunday’s comeback victory over Bournemouth.

The signing of the former Spain Under-21 international – who spent a decade with Barca until 2023 – will take Newcastle’s spending north of £200m.

Goalkeepers Lukas Hornicek and Ewen Jaouen have also been joined by Bazoumana Toure, Aladji Bamba, Amar Dedic and Steur – while Anthony Gordon departed to Barcelona for £75m.

Sports.title: Arsenal transfer blow as left winger target Kenan Yildiz suffers major injury with Gabriel Martinelli in £60m exit talks
Sports.content:
ARSENAL’S chances of signing Kenan Yildiz have taken another hit after the winger suffered an injury at the weekend.

The Gunners are looking to bring in attacking reinforcements before next week’s transfer deadline, but a move for Yildiz now seems extremely unlikely.



Mikel Arteta is a big fan of Yildiz and the club are actively trying to strengthen their left wing position.

However, the 21-year-old ace was forced off with a foot injury in the 69th minute of Juventus‘ 1-0 win over Frosinone on Sunday.



Reports in Italy suggest that the issue could be serious, with surgery not ruled out and Yildiz potentially facing up to two months on the sidelines.

A lengthy injury would make Arsenal moving for Yildiz even more unlikely this summer.



Juventus have been clear in their stance that Yildiz is not for sale anyway.

Manager Luciano Spaletti has said he is “calm” about the future of his star player.

Speaking on Saturday, he said: “I experience it calmly because the player is Yildiz. From my point of view, it’s simple, they can offer whatever they want, I want to be able to field Yildiz next season.

“Yildiz is a guy who is perfect to have mature conversations with. And consequently, he knows very well that he shouldn’t rush anything, that he shouldn’t speed anything up.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“His future is already important at Juventus.”

Arsenal could be a left winger short if they do not bring in a new face before the transfer deadline.

Gabriel Martinelli is in talks with Saudi Arabian side Al Hilal after being left out of the squad for both of Arsenal’s 3-0 wins over Manchester City and Coventry.

The Brazilian could end his seven-year stint in North London if Al Hilal are willing to cough up a fee close to the £60m figure Arsenal are seeking.



Arsenal rejected a £38m bid for Martinelli from Turkish club Galatasaray earlier in the window, but are open to selling the 25-year-old.

Martinelli is in the final year of his contract with Arsenal, but the Gunners hold an option for a further 12 months.

Arteta has already brought in Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge in a £34m deal this summer.



Tzolis, 24, has hit the ground running with two eye-catching performances against Man City and Coventry, but will have little backup if the Gunners can’t bring in another left winger in the next week.

Arsenal had been interested in both Vinicius Junior and Morgan Rogers earlier in the window, but failed to get either deal over the line.

Sports.title: Paris Saint-Germain ticket and hotel deals for Ligue 1 games in new season from only £319pp at Parc des Princes
Sports.content:
FOOTBALL fans can look forward to the ultimate city break in Paris with a unbeatable trip to the French capital to see the superstars of PSG.

Official ticket and hotel packages to watch Champions League winners Paris Saint-Germain have gone on sale.

Sports.title: Is £130m Alvarez an upgrade on Gyokeres? In many ways yes, but Arsenal will miss parts of their current striker’s game
Sports.content:
JULIAN ALVAREZ could be the final piece of Mikel Arteta’s Arsenal jigsaw, but the stats suggest Viktor Gyokeres would leave some pretty big boots to fill.

The Gunners are ready to make a move for the Atletico Madrid and Argentina star in the final week of the transfer window if they get encouragement from either the player or his club that a deal can actually be done.



Although Alvarez is said to prefer a move to Barcelona, Atletico have strongly resisted the idea of selling him to their La Liga rivals – report The Athletic.

That potentially leaves the door open for a move to Arsenal, with some reports suggesting that they could even throw Gyokeres in as part of a sensational player plus cash offer.



The Gunners are prepared to go beyond their club-record £105million fee that they paid to sign Declan Rice from West Ham in 2023, with Atletico reportedly wanting as much as £130m to even consider selling their star man.

Alvarez was booed yesterday when his name was read out before Atletico’s 2-2 draw with Villarreal and was jeered again when he came on as a 66th-minute substitute.

That backlash could yet force Atletico to soften their stance – particularly with reports in Spain suggesting Alvarez’s position on only wanting Barcelona is beginning to change.

The former Manchester City man is still hoping for that dream move, but crucially, he is no longer thought to be completely closing the door on a return to the Premier League.

Gary Neville certainly believes Alvarez would take the Gunners, and indeed captain Martin Odegaard‘s game, to another level.

After Arsenal’s 3-0 win against Coventry on Friday night, eight-time Premier League winner Neville told Sky Sports: “What a squad [Mikel Arteta] has built. If he puts another forward into that, if they could get Julian Alvarez somehow, that would light this place up as you’d have a world-class striker to go with all the world-class defenders and midfielders.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“They wouldn’t just become Premier League title winners they’d go the next step and win a Champions League. He needs a bit of magic up front – someone that can win a game for you when you don’t play well.

“Odegaard is exceptional. If there was an Ian Wright-type player up front for Arsenal who makes those short runs he’d be even better.

“As [Kai] Havertz and [Viktor] Gyokeres always come to the ball, Odegaard has to play possession rather than playing the slip passes. If Arsenal were to sign Julian Alvarez then he’d go up a level as it would be perfect for the style of play.”

There is certainly an argument for that as Alvarez is more creative than Gyokeres, registering ten assists last season compared with the Swede’s three.



His 127 minutes per goal or assist also beats Gyokeres’ 145, but that is where the idea of Alvarez being a straightforward upgrade starts to become a little more complicated.

Gyokeres scored 21 goals in 3,481 minutes, while Alvarez managed 20 in 3,549 minutes – meaning the Arsenal man was more prolific in terms of minutes per goal — 165.7 compared with Alvarez’s 190.5.

Gyokeres, who only signed for Arsenal last summer for £55m from Sporting Lisbon, also had a superior shot conversion rate, scoring with 22.6 per cent of his efforts compared with Alvarez’s 15.9 per cent.

There was a period between December and February when Alvarez went 11 games without scoring – something which clearly damaged his goals-per-minute and conversion rate numbers.



The idea that Alvarez simply lives in the space behind defenders is also not quite the complete picture.

Although he can make clever runs in behind, Alvarez also likes to come towards the ball and get involved in build-up play – something he showed with Argentina at the World Cup when he often dropped deeper to allow Lionel Messi to stay higher up the pitch.

That helps explain why his passing accuracy is a whopping 82.8 per cent compared with Gyokeres’ 63.8 per cent.

In that sense, Alvarez can be more of a Harry Kane-style striker – dropping deep, linking play and dragging defenders around, while having the ability to get on the end of things too.

His low centre of gravity also makes him incredibly difficult to knock off the ball and helps explain why he completed 65 dribbles last season compared with just 13 for Gyokeres.



But if Alvarez does come with Gyokeres heading in the other direction, what Arsenal would lose is equally important.

Gyokeres is 6ft 2in, while Alvarez is only 5ft 7in – a physical difference that is reflected in their aerial numbers.

Gyokeres won 44 aerial duels compared with just 13 for Alvarez.

The Swede also won considerably more fouls – 54 to 32 – as his power and physicality makes him a nightmare for defenders.



Perhaps the biggest surprise is possession won in the final third.

Alvarez has a reputation as a pressing monster, but Gyokeres actually won more possession in the final third last season – 34 times compared with Alvarez’s 31.

Gyokeres also recorded more touches in the opposition box – 219 to Alvarez’s 198.

Alvarez did, however, take more shots – 126 to Gyokeres’ 93 – largely because of the way he becomes involved in more phases of the attack by dropping deep.

So, Neville’s prediction that Alvarez would be the perfect fit is not necessarily wrong.



However, the statistics suggest it isn’t quite as simple as swapping one striker for another and watching Arsenal improve across the board.

Arteta could give Alvarez a slightly different role, asking him to prioritise making more runs beyond the defence.

If that happens, Alvarez’s movement could indeed take the Gunners up another level – as Neville eluded to.

But it would also mean sacrificing the aerial threat, physical presence and penalty-box dominance that Gyokeres brings.



Arteta’s caveat to that could be that he also has Havertz, who brings the same qualities.

Alvarez, on the other hand, would give Arsenal something different – a more rounded footballer who offers more creativity.

But Gyokeres was the more efficient goalscorer last season and provides qualities Alvarez simply does not possess.

The numbers, therefore, suggest Alvarez is an upgrade in some ways, rather than the complete upgrade many expect.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

For Arsenal, the question is whether Arteta values what Alvarez adds more than what he would lose by replacing Gyokeres.



With just eight days of the transfer window left, that could be the £130m question which decides whether the Gunners make one final blockbuster move.

Furious Leandro Trossard hits out at officials after ex-Arsenal star SLAPPED in game

Leandro Trossard is getting to grips with life in Turkey after leaving Arsenal last month but was embroiled in controversy during Besiktas' loss to Alanyaspor on Sunday

View Image Leandro Trossard was struck by an opponent during Besiktas' 1-0 loss to Alanyaspor

Leandro Trossard and Besiktas have condemned the 'disgraceful' refereeing in their match with Alanyaspor after an opposition player evaded punishment despite appearing to slap the former Arsenal attacker in the face.

‌



Trossard completed a transfer to the Turkish Super Lig last month and Sunday's 1-0 defeat to Alanyaspor was just his second league game for Besiktas. Unfortunately, the 32-year-old was involved in the major talking point of the match for all the wrong reasons after getting caught up in an off the ball incident with Fidan Aliti.

‌



Video replays showed the Swiss defender clearly struck Trossard in the face after a coming together - but he was spared punishment by referee Adnan Deniz Kayatepe and VAR, much to the shock of the Belgium international.

‌



Trossard fumed after the game: "The decision should clearly have been changed; I think the opponent slapped me. Clear red card. The decision needed to be changed."

Sports.title: Fans burned and injured after fireworks thrown in shocking Dutch league match
Sports.content:
Fans burned and injured after fireworks thrown in shocking Dutch league match

Seven supporters were left with burns as well as damage to their hearing and vision after away fans let off fireworks inside the stadium midway through a match

View 2 Images Feyenoord goalkeeper Tjark Ernst narrowly avoided being hit by a firework during the disturbance (Image: Getty Images)

SC Cambuur have confirmed seven of their supporters were injured by fireworks set off from the away section during their Eredivisie home match against Feyenoord. The club from Leeuwarden state that their injuries range from burns to hearing and vision damage after a large-scale setting off of fireworks from the Kooi Stadion's south stand.

‌



Cambuur's initial statement on Sunday evening listed the number of injuries as five. An update on Monday afternoon then increased that total by two to seven.

‌



Play was paused in the 12th minute for 10 minutes due to the disruption. Feyenoord went on to win 5-2.

‌



The statement shared on Sunday evening reads: "What should have been a football party between SC Cambuur and Feyenoord was marred in the twelfth minute this afternoon by the large-scale setting off of fireworks. From the away section in the South stand, Feyenoord 'supporters' not only set off fireworks, but also fired towards the field and the surrounding stands.

"Five injured supporters are to be regretted with burns, hearing damage and eye damage as the main injuries. It goes without saying that all care and attention goes out to these injured supporters, and everyone at the club sympathises enormously.

"The match was eventually resumed after a strike of about ten minutes, and this is in line with the protocols of the KNVB and in consultation with the parties involved. It should be clear that setting off and firing fireworks is completely unacceptable and in no way belongs in a football stadium. Together with the authorities, we will do everything in our power to track down and punish the perpetrators."

‌



View 2 Images Fireworks were thrown onto the pitch and into other sections of supporters (Image: Getty Images)

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

They then added in an update barely 24 hours later: "Following on from the message below, we can now unfortunately report that not five, but seven supporters fell victim to the fireworks from the away section yesterday afternoon at the match between SC Cambuur and Feyenoord.

‌



"There has now been personal contact with six of these victims, and we would also like to get in touch with the seventh person to provide appropriate aftercare and to assist with advice and assistance.

"In addition, there will also be an official report from the club towards the perpetrators. The search for these people is in full swing under the leadership of Feyenoord, and in cooperation with all parties involved. A new update will follow later this week."

Feyenoord general manager Robert Eenhoorn also condemned the incident. He said: "It is of course especially terrible for a number of injured Cambuur supporters. I don't understand the reason either, because normally you hear something in advance.

‌



"It's also not the first time that something like this happens in the away section. It would be a shame for the benevolent supporters if we are punished with an empty away section.

"Our own goalkeeper gets a rocket at him and can just avoid him."

Sports.content:
William Saliba sent brutal warning after shock Arsenal transfer - 'He doesn't get back in'

Arsenal defender William Saliba played a key role for the Gunners last season as they ended their long wait for a Premier League crown but John Terry has claimed his place in the team is under threat

View 2 Images William Saliba is currently out with a back issue (Image: Getty Images)

John Terry has claimed that William Saliba will remain on the sidelines following Arsenal’s signing of Ezri Konsa. The Frenchman played a key role last summer as the Gunners claimed the Premier League title.

‌



But he missed the opening game of the current campaign having undergone surgery for a back issue. Cristhian Mosquera played in his place, while Piero Hincapie was in reserve.

‌



Arsenal also added to their centre-back options last week, having confirmed a deal to sign Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa. Having been in the Midlands at the same time as the England man, Terry has claimed that Saliba might face a tough time of things as he attempts to win his place back.

‌



Asked by the FC Bullard TikTok channel who he believes is the best value signing of the summer, the Chelsea icon replied: “I would go Ezri Konsa for Arsenal.

“That’s a massive signing. I think even when William Saliba is back fit, he doesn’t get back in the Arsenal team, I think Ezri Konsa is that good.

‌



“I worked with him at Aston Villa and he’s so aggressive but also happy to play on the halfway line because if it goes in behind he’s quick enough to get there and recover. He’s a really, really good player.”

Saliba, 25, has been an Arsenal player since 2019, but has only been a first-team regular for the past four seasons after loan spells with Saint-Etienne, Nice and Marseille. In the meantime, Konsa has been a key player for Villa, with the Midlands side having won the Europa League and enjoyed three seasons in Europe under Unai Emery.

Asked what the defender would offer to his side, Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta said: “When I look at squads, some clubs still have incredible and much bigger squads than us. We just look to improve and do what’s right for us, and look at players we already have who can improve us. Ezri is certainly a player we really liked in the defensive line.”

Meanwhile, Konsa has already spoken out on his role in the side and said he would be willing to play in any position that his new manager asks.

He said: “I like to build up from the back and I like to have a lot of the ball. It's Mikel's style and from what I've seen from games, it's the same way the defenders here play. So hopefully I can add a little bit more.

“It's good being versatile. I can do both jobs, right-back and centre-back, but for me ultimately, wherever the manager wants to put me is, I’ll always do a job and do my best.”

Sports.title: Alexander Isak 'pretended he wasn't bothered' but Newcastle fans 'clearly upset him'
Sports.content:
Alexander Isak 'pretended he wasn't bothered' but Newcastle fans 'clearly upset him'

Liverpool striker Alexander Isak endured a tough time upon his return to St James' Park on Sunday

View 2 Images Alexander Isak was targeted by Newcastle fans on Sunday (Image: 2026 Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA)

It wasn't the return to St James' Park that Alexander Isak would have envisaged as Liverpool were held to a 2-2 draw at Newcastle United on Sunday. The Swedish star left the Magpies for the Reds last summer in a £125million deal, which stands as the British transfer record.

‌



Isak's expensive departure was acrimonious to say the least after he downed tools in order to engineer his move to Anfield. So, the stage was perhaps set for the forward to dish out retribution after he was verbally abused by sections of the Newcastle faithful upon arrival at his former stomping ground on Sunday afternoon.

‌



The Swedish international was jeered heavily when he left the Liverpool team coach to enter the stadium, with chants of 'rat' audible. Loud whistles and boos also accompanied his every touch during the game as he struggled to impose himself on proceedings.

‌



A body language expert has claimed Isak, upon arrival at Newcastle, was eager to "get away" from the fans who used to adore him. He's also been accused of trying to act as if he was unbothered by the hostility, when he "clearly was."

Darren Stanton said via OLBG: "Alexander Isak does something called lip suppression when he first arrives at St. James' Park. His lips are closed, pierced and slightly compressed. There's no arrival smile or anything like that from someone who is returning to his former home ground. He's very aware of the reception he's receiving and what is being chanted.

Virgil van Dijk sends Liverpool chiefs transfer message with Andoni Iraola in agreement READ MORE :

"The next thing I notice is that his eyebrows are slightly lowered, and he's looking downwards before entering the ground. This actually shows he wants to get away from the Newcastle fans as quickly as possible.

‌



"He's trying to act like he's not bothered by it, but he clearly is. When people don't look around, they try to imply that they are not bothered and that they don't care. It wouldn't surprise me if he wasn't actually listening to any music at all!

Sports.title: FIFA legends say 'enough is enough' as they tear into Gianni Infantino with bombshell statement
Sports.content:
FIFA legends say 'enough is enough' as they tear into Gianni Infantino with bombshell statement

Gianni Infantino has seen calls for his job as FIFA president after a highly-controversial summer, and now, a number of footballing legends have put the pressure on

View Image Gianni Infantino has been hit with criticism (Image: Getty Images)

A number of FIFA legends, including Robert Pires and Juan Sebastian Veron have said that "enough is enough," citing how football has lost core values under Gianni Infantino's leadership in a bombshell statement. The Swiss president of FIFA has come under fire following a controversial World Cup in North America, coupled with plans to sell shares of the tournament to the highest bidder.

‌



Just a matter of weeks ago, Infantino revealed plans for a scheme dubbed the FIFA Forward Enterprise, which was quickly condemned by fans of the beautiful game, as well as continental governing bodies. UEFA even went as far as boycotting world football's most prestigious tournament if Infantino's vision came to fruition.

‌



As a result, the FFE was canned altogether, with Infantino scrambling to mend broken relationships worldwide. And now, a number of footballing legends have vowed to make a difference, refusing to sit in silence as the game loses meaning.

‌

Gianni Infantino losing grip on FIFA as Ireland's FA release statement in another blow READ MORE :

In a statement shared on social media, a cohort of players wrote: "As players, football has given us everything, and we have given our lives to it. Between us, we have played on its greatest stages and worn our national shirts with pride.

"But we know that none of our achievements would’ve been possible without the fans, whose passion and commitment is the foundation of this game. We share the exact same concerns as the millions of fans around the world.

"Like them, we have watched the game we love drift away from its core values under FIFA’s current leadership. For too long, we’ve seen major decisions taken without players being consulted or considered, and without any regard for the fans who sustain the sport.

‌



"Change is necessary. Power has blurred the current leadership’s ability to distinguish between its own interests and what is best for football. Recent events have made silence impossible. Enough is enough.

Sports.title: Ollie Watkins transfer saga has turned ugly - but loyalty is a two-way street
Sports.content:
Ollie Watkins transfer saga has turned ugly - but loyalty is a two-way street

Ollie Watkins' time at Aston Villa could be up with the player supposedly choosing not to play on Sunday - but clubs and players can be equally disloyal when it suits them

View 3 Images Ollie Watkins looks to be trying to force Aston Villa's hand (Image: Molly Darlington/Getty Images)

The transfer window can be a particularly bruising time for players, egos and reputations. And there is unlikely to be too much sympathy from Aston Villa fans for Ollie Watkins after Unai Emery ’s post-match comments.

‌



Villa lose 4-0 at Brighton, the club has been left in a bit of a mess (again) by a messy transfer window which has seen big-name departures like Youri Tielemans, Ezri Konsa, Lucas Digne and Morgan Rogers with Emiliano Martinez likely to follow.

‌



So, the Watkins story - a live transfer target for Saudi Pro League club Al Hilal - certainly meant people are talking about the Villa striker rather than a humiliating defeat. A distraction tactic?

‌



It has made Watkins the villain of the piece with Emery hinting heavily - but not quite saying it out right - that the England striker refused to play at Brighton.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Watkins, 30, is being offered a huge contract in the Saudi Pro League, it would be a fantastic pay day for a player who has reached the very top in his career having really battled his way up from non-league. This is a really nice, understated but determined player who does not really seek the spotlight but there have been ups and downs at Villa.

‌



It has largely always been up when he is on the pitch because he works hard, scores goals and gives his all for the team. He has enjoyed success with the Europa League and helping the club qualify for the Champions League.

The downs have been when he has been dropped, he has been left out on numerous occasions and when players are axed from the team no-one stands up for them.

It’s just when the suggestion comes they don’t want to play for the team. Emery is such a good manager and one of the reasons is because he’s a bad loser. He’s so determined to win. As the saying goes, show me a good loser and I’ll show you a loser. Emery is a winner.

‌



View 3 Images Unai Emery didn't shy away from addressing Ollie Watkins' situation (Image: Joris Verwijst/Soccrates/Getty Images)

After the Brighton game, you could see he was fuming, Watkins was caught in the crossfire and is now public enemy No.1. It was Villa who denied Watkins a move to Arsenal in January 2025 when the Midlands club did need to sell. Arsenal will always say that it was Villa who first sounded them out. Villa eventually sold Jhon Duran to balance the books.

Watkins was priced out of a move but, like all players, is a commodity who is owned by his club - until they don’t want him. Then he’s just discarded. Villa have sold so many players this summer that it must have created some uncertainty. If you look at what happened last season - they did not win any of their first five Premier League games and scored just one goal - this transfer carousel is not new.

‌



They have been prolific buyers and sellers. And so is Watkins so wrong? There is no way a player should go on strike to force a move when they are paid so well in the first place.

View 3 Images Morgan Rogers is one of several high profile sales made by Aston Villa (Image: Darren Walsh, Chelsea FC via Getty Images)

But is it always that black and white? You can be sure players up and down the country will be talking with their clubs, agents and managers about what the future holds.

‌



Many players will feel as if they need to move on. This is not the era of player power. But we have seen a shift of more clubs openly courting transfer targets - even if they are under contract.

Every club does it and if that turns the odd head - especially when a move would be for life-changing money - then they probably are not in the right frame of mind to play.

But equally, the player will probably recall the last time they were dropped and ask their own questions about loyalty. It must be a two-way street. Clearly, Villa fans might not agree right now. But this saga has probably happened at every club this summer - but not so publicly.

Sports.title: 'We haven't got the money' - Wolff says Mercedes can't match rivals' upgrade rate
Sports.content:
Toto Wolff says Mercedes do not have extra money available to quickly respond to the growing threat from McLaren and Ferrari through car development.

The Silver Arrows continue to lead both world championship races, and grew their leads in both standings across the Dutch Grand Prix Sprint weekend, but have seen their early-season dominance eroded in recent months.

After winning the opening six rounds of F1's new rules era, Mercedes have won two races in the last six, the same number as Ferrari and McLaren.

McLaren have taken the last two wins after upgrades to their car at each of the last two events, while Mercedes have brought only smaller revisions to their W17 since its last big update at the Canadian GP in late May.

All teams operate to a yearly budget cap governing car spend, which for 2026 was raised to $215m due to the huge change in regulations, and have to decide how they each allocate spend on car development through the season.

Wolff suggested Mercedes' approach to the full year meant they could not accelerate any upgrades - or bring more - to their W17 earlier than already scheduled to counter what their chief rivals were doing.

"We haven't got the money to put developments on the car," he said.

"And I said it before that we are trying to evenly split that through the season based on our calculations of when we can bring the biggest updates and optimising the championship points.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Dutch Grand Prix

"But we just can do what we can do. That's why it is a development race. If you bring an update, each of the top teams will have a couple of tenths in it, at least, and that's what we lose.

"The ride has been a bit tougher than at the beginning of the year."

Put to him that Ferrari and McLaren seemed to have the money, Wolff said: "You will see towards the end of the season whether they are going to be able to deploy as much stuff on to the car as they do now.

"Someone might have a different strategy in spending more at the beginning and then in the middle of the year than towards the end."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mercedes team-mates Kimi Antonelli and George Russell reflect on their Dutch Grand Prix race

Wolff did not explicitly state why Mercedes were not able to match their rivals' current rate of bringing upgrades to the track.

He was asked whether they had forward-loaded their development spend to ensure they had started the season and F1's new era of rules most strongly.

They won all six of the opening races - and have still remained a victory contender at most other rounds too - although reliability problems proved costly over the first half of the campaign with the loss of likely big points alone through driver retirements in Montreal, Barcelona and Silverstone.

"Did we spend much at the beginning in the initial development? I don't think so," replied Wolff. "I just think we're an organisation and we have a certain size and infrastructure.

"In that respect, we had a very quick car. We left between 50 to 100 points on the table with reliability issues. That would have given us more of a gap than we have today.

"Other than that, we are continuing to execute that the plan was and what the financial realities mean for us."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Antonelli storms past Lando Norris to take the lead in the Dutch Grand Prix on the restart

When the Mercedes counterpart's comments were put to him after Sunday's race, McLaren chief Andrea Stella said he suspected their Brackley rivals still had plenty up their sleeve for the title run-in.

"I would like to believe you, but I actually don't believe it," said Stella.

"Thanks to the 2027 power-unit regulations [which will see a change in the power ratio], all teams will have an allowance in their reporting for the cost cap. If I'm not wrong, it's $3m that you can use in the 2026 reporting for the cost cap calculations.

"And I'm sure that Mercedes, having seen that the rivals are kind of elevating the game, I'm sure they will now cash in on their development that surely is happening in the ground.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Norris hunted down Antonelli and Lewis Hamilton to take the race lead at the Dutch Grand Prix

"I'm sure their car in the wind tunnel is quite a bit faster than the car they have on track. And they will want to now convert some of this potential into upgrades that make it to the real car.

"So I'm pretty sure that they will have upgrades. Obviously, it would be good if not, but I don't even want to think it."

Russell, Antonelli hopeful over next Mercedes upgrades

Mercedes' drivers Kimi Antonelli and George Russell finished the Zandvoort race in second and third places respectively behind McLaren's race-winning Lando Norris, who has now won back-to-back events either side of F1's summer break.

Russell said: "I don't think it's a major surprise for us, seeing how competitive Lando was this weekend, considering he won in Budapest.

"It's a very similar circuit with the long corners, high tyre degradation, with the two-stop strategy, so there's a lot of similarities between the two circuits.

"This may continue for the coming two or three races until we start to bring more to the car, and fingers crossed our competitors don't."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch Russell win the Dutch Grand Prix Sprint, as Norris loses second place to Charles Leclerc

Antonelli, who still increased his overall championship lead over Russell and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton to 59 points, added: "We're clearly not the fastest car anymore on the grid.

"We're probably second or third, at least in today's race, and McLaren has taken a huge step, especially since Hungary, since the big upgrade package they brought.

"But I'm confident with the team. You know, the team has been working super hard on this next package that is coming up, and they just want to make sure that it's going to work out well once we put it on."

The high-speed straights and tight chicanes of Monza at the Italian Grand Prix next week will represent a different challenge for the front-runners compared with the last two venues and Russell is hopeful Mercedes "will be slightly more competitive there".

He added: "Monza may be slightly different, but I think they [McLaren] are the team to beat right now."

Sports.title: When are the Europa and Conference League draws and how do they work?
Sports.content:
The Europa League and Conference League league phase draws will see British clubs - including Bournemouth, Sunderland, Crystal Palace - discover their opponents.

When is the draw?

The Europa League league phase draw - involving Bournemouth, Sunderland and Crystal Palace - takes place at 12pm UK time on Friday. The Conference League draw - which could involve Brighton, Hearts, Hibs, Motherwell, Rangers and Northern Irish team Larne - gets under way straight after.

Who is in Europa League?

Twelve teams qualify directly for the league phase of the Europa League, with one slot also reserved for UEFA Conference League title holders, Crystal Palace.

Image: Crystal Palace goalkeeper Dean Henderson lifts the UEFA Europa Conference League trophy last season

A further 12 sides secure their places by qualifying through the play-off round. The 36-team line-up is completed by 11 losing teams transferring from the UEFA Champions League third qualifying round and play-offs.

Qualified teams: AC Milan, AZ Alkmaar, Bayer Leverkusen, Bournemouth, Celta Vigo, Crystal Palace, Hoffenheim, Juventus, Marseille, Olympiacos, Real Sociedad, Rennes, Sparta Prague, Sturm Graz, Sunderland, Torreense, Union Saint-Gilloise

Teams who could play Europa League if they lose in the Champions League play-off round: AEK Athens, Bodo/Glimt, Celje, Celtic, Dinamo Zagreb, Fenerbahce, Hapoel Beer-Sheva, LASK, Levski Sofia, Lyon, NEC Breda, Sabah, Slovan Bratislava, Viking Stavanger.

Teams who could play Europa League if they win in the Europa Lague play-off round: Aarhus, Anderlecht, Ararat-Armenia, Benfica, Besiktas, Crvena Zvezda, CSKA Sofia, Egnatia, Ferencvaros, Iberia Tblisi, Jagiellonia, Kairat Almaty, Kauno Zalgiris, Lech Poznan, Lillestrom, Mjallby, OFI Crete, Omonia, Salzburg, Sint-Truidense, Thun, Trabzonspor, Union Craiova, Viktoria Plzen.

Who is in Conference League?

All 36 teams enter the league phase via qualifying, with none directly through.

Teams who could play Conference League if they win in the Conference League play-off round: Ajax, Atalanta, Austria Vienna, Borac, Braga, Brann, Brighton, FC Copenhagen, Dinamo City, Drita, Freiburg, Gent, Getafe, Gornik Zabrze, Hapoel Tel-Aviv, Hajduk Split, Hearts, Hibernian, Hradec Kralove, Inter Escaldes, Inter Turku, Jablonec, Klaksvik, Kups Kuopio, Lincoln Red Imps, Larne, Lugano, Maccabi Tel-Aviv, Midtjylland, Monaco, Motherwell, Nordsjaelland, Pafos, Panathinaikos, PAOK, Partizan, Qarabag, Rakow, Rangers, Riga, Rijeka, Shamrock Rovers, Sion, SK Rapid, St Gallen, Tromso, Twente, Vikingur Rekjavik.

Teams who could play Conference League if they lose in the Europa League play-off round: Aarhus, Anderlecht, Ararat-Armenia, Benfica, Besiktas, Crvena Zvezda, CSKA Sofia, Egnatia, Ferencvaros, Iberia Tblisi, Jagiellonia, Kairat Almaty, Kauno Zalgiris, Lech Poznan, Lillestrom, Mjallby, OFI Crete, Omonia, Salzburg, Sint-Truidense, Thun, Trabzonspor, Union Craiova, Viktoria Plzen.

Image: The Europa League and Conference League trophies

How does the league phase work in the Europa League and Conference League?

In the Europa League, every club is guaranteed a minimum of eight league-stage games against eight different opponents, with four games home and four away.

In the Conference League though, each side will face six different teams, with three games at home and three away.

In both tournaments, the top eight sides in the league will qualify automatically for the knockout stages, while the teams finishing in ninth to 24th place will compete in a two-legged play-off to secure a place in the last 16 of the competition.

Teams ranked 25-36 are eliminated from all competitions.

How many teams can you face from any one nation?

In the league phase, teams cannot face opponents from their own country and can face a maximum of two sides from the same country.

Image: Aston Villa won the Europa League last season and now take part in the Champions League

When are the league phase games?

Europa League

Matchday 1: September 16/17

Matchday 2: October 15

Matchday 3: October 22

Matchday 4: November 5

Matchday 5: November 26

Matchday 6: December 10

Matchday 7: January 21, 2027

Matchday 8: January 28, 2027

Conference League

Matchday 1: October 15

Matchday 2: October 22

Matchday 3: November 5

Matchday 4: November 26

Matchday 5: December 10

Matchday 6: December 17

The key dates

The 2026/27 Europa League final will take place on May 26, 2027 at the Stadion Frankfurt in Germany, while the Conference League final is scheduled for June 2, 2025 at Besiktas Park in Istanbul.

Europa League

Knockout round play-offs: February 18 & 25, 2027

Round of 16: March 11 & 18, 2027

Quarter-finals: April 8 & 15, 2027

Semi-finals: April 29 & May 6, 2027

Final: May 26, 2027 (Stadion Frankfurt, Germany)

Conference League

Knockout round play-offs: February 18 & 25, 2027

Round of 16: March 11 & 18, 2027

Quarter-finals: April 8 & 15, 2027

Semi-finals: April 29 & May 6, 2027

Final: June 2, 2027 (Besiktas Park, Istanbul, Turkey)

Sports.title: Don't panic! Why Man Utd and Carrick get a pass after flat Hull defeat
Sports.content:
I was at the game on Saturday and it was clear early on in the game that Manchester United were not at the races against Hull City.

Words will be bandied towards Michael Carrick's side this week until their home game against Ipswich on Sunday; for example, a lack of intensity, aggression and intent on display.

But when I left Hull, I just felt it was a bit more nuanced than that.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the Premier League match between Hull and Manchester United

It was a bad performance, for sure. Carrick's side didn't perform, and only he will truly know why, but from the off it was quite clear some of his main players are not quite up to match sharpness compared to where they will be in a few weeks.

Six of Carrick's first-team players did have a full pre-season. But Carrick also had a new midfield duo playing together in Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos.

Manchester United

Ipswich Town Sunday 30th August 4:00pm Kick off 4:30pm

Off the bench, he had players nowhere near full fitness in Benjamin Sesko (has not played a minute of pre-season), as well as Kobbie Mainoo and Marcus Rashford, who have had limited minutes since returning from England duty in the summer.

Hull also deserve enormous credit for being a well-drilled outfit for their first Premier League game in nine years while also having a squad who have experienced a full pre-season to prepare for their opener.

Also, allow me a moment to myth-bust something I have seen across social media over the last few days since the defeat.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Michael Carrick promises improvements in his Manchester United side following their surprise opening-day defeat to Hull City, but insists that he won't change the way he does things

'Four defeats out of five under Michael Carrick have come against sides who have played a back five'

Not having it. Look at the games!

Two of them were pre-season games, including United's first of the summer against Wrexham and their last against Ruben Amorim's AC Milan. If anyone is using these as barometers of a side struggling against a formation, it is simply not right.

Hull was bad. Leeds at Old Trafford last season was also bad. These two performances share a lot of similarities but I would argue the most common denominator is that I left both games thinking they were seriously lacking from a physical point of view and that will be Carrick's most pressing thought.

I am more than willing, and Carrick has more than deserved, somewhat of a pass for the Hull result, and I would be extremely surprised if United were not considerably improved against Ipswich Town on Sunday.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan gives us his three things to take away from Manchester United's loss to Hull City on the opening day of the season

So what are Man Utd's plans for the remainder of the transfer window?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look as Sky Sports' William Bitibiri explains exactly what Carlos Baleba might bring to Manchester United's midfield

The midfield was Manchester United's priority going into the season and they have gone some way to addressing it by spending over £150m in reinforcements, with Carlos Baleba the latest addition to their ranks.

But United find themselves in a similar situation to last summer - reinforcing your greatest need just highlights your next biggest gap within the squad.

Rewind back to 2025: the club had finally addressed their inefficiency up front by adding Benjamin Sesko, Matheus Cunha and Bryan Mbeumo but having sorted the attacking weaponry, it became even more obvious the midfield needed strengthening.

United waited 12 months as they did not want to sign a stop-gap midfielder for the sake of addressing the area and believed they would have a better run at the midfield market the following summer.

There is a similar feeling now when it comes to left-back. Now United have signed their three midfielders, the need for a left-back is a must.

The club have long admired Myles Lewis-Skelly and Lewis Hall and my feeling is they are top of United's list in that position.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Danyal Khan looks at whether Manchester United are better off waiting until next year to ensure they sign a No 1 target at left-back

Both seem unattainable at this moment in time, with managers of both clubs dismissing any chances of their players leaving. In addition to Bruno Guimaraes' injury, which especially seems to all but rule out a potential departure for Lewis-Skelly.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mikel Arteta says he is '100 per cent' sure that Myles Lewis-Skelly will be staying at Arsenal after the transfer window closes and is unsure if Bruno Guimaraes will be available against Coventry

My feeling is that with United having focused on attack and midfield over the last two summer windows, they are willing to wait until next summer to address their defence - including a first-choice left-back when Luke Shaw's contract expires next summer.

Things could change of course, and I would not completely rule out United getting creative in terms of potentially adding a left-back in the last week of the window but at the moment, it seems unlikely.

Barcelona's Alejandro Balde has been the latest player linked with United at left-back but from what I understand, although United are aware of his situation in Catalonia, it is not a name they are strongly pursuing at this time.

All in all, it is a lot of pressure on Luke Shaw to stay fit all season, and some reliance will need to be put on Patrick Dorgu at left-back. The club see his long-term future in that position.

Noussair Mazraoui and Diogo Dalot can also both deputise in that position too.

In terms of departures at United, at the time of writing, it seems unlikely any first-team players will leave the club before the deadline.

One potential departure this window was Dutch forward Joshua Zirzkee but interest from Italy has yet to materialise into anything concrete and he is expected to stay at the club.
