World.title: Trump administration seeks to formalise H-1B fee of more than $100,000
World.content:
The new proposal would charge $103,265 for H-1B visas, and attempts to make permanent a temporary rule challenged by the US courts.

The administration of United States President Donald Trump has proposed a rule to formalise a controversial fee for H-1B work visas to the US and charge $103,265 for these visa applications going forward.

The proposed fee for highly skilled foreign workers was published in the US Federal Register on Monday, and will now be subject to a 30-day public comment period, after which it could be finalised and put into practice by the Department of Homeland Security (DHS). It would dramatically increase the cost of visas that are in high use in recruiting workers in the tech, education and research sectors.

Last year, Trump temporarily imposed a fee of $100,000 for the visa programme, which was then blocked by court rulings. The temporary proclamation is due to expire in September, and the new DHS proposal would replace it and make the fee permanent.

In June, a federal judge ruled the fee was illegal and barred the Trump administration from collecting it. A Boston-based appeals court is reviewing that decision, while a different court considers whether a judge in Washington, DC properly rejected a challenge to the fee by a major business group.

The H-1B programme allows US employers to hire foreign workers with training in specialty fields and offers 65,000 visas annually, with another 20,000 for workers with advanced degrees, approved for three to six years.

The order Trump issued last year sharply increased the cost of obtaining some H-1B visas, which had typically come with about $2,000 to $5,000 in fees, depending on various factors.



The increase in fees has discouraged H-1B visa requests, according to court filings. As of February 15, US Citizenship and Immigration Services had received from 70 employers just 85 payments of the $100,000 fee, the administration said in a March filing.

Debate over visa programme

Trump, a Republican, and other critics of the H-1B programme say it is abused by many companies who replace US workers with cheaper foreign labour.

But business groups and many individual companies have said the visa programme is needed to address a lack of qualified American workers ⁠for some jobs and to allow US businesses to recruit top talent.

In imposing the fee, Trump invoked the president’s power under federal immigration law to restrict the entry of certain foreign nationals who would be detrimental to US interests.

The fee is being challenged by the US Chamber of Commerce, the largest US business lobbying group, Democratic-led states, and a coalition ⁠of unions and employers. Those lawsuits could be amended to challenge the rule proposed this week once it is finalised.

Legal challenges mount

The lawsuits claim that Trump’s power to restrict entry does not allow him to override the law ⁠that created the H-1B visa programme. The states and groups that sued also say that DHS cannot impose fees, taxes or other means to generate revenue for the US without permission from Congress.

The Trump administration has maintained that the fee is not a traditional tax and that courts have little power to question the president’s authority to restrict entry into the country.

Amid Trump’s broader immigration crackdown, employers last year registered for about 344,000 H-1B visas, down ‌more than 25 percent from 2024, and fewer than half of the 794,000 visas sought in 2023, according to data from US Citizenship and Immigration Services.

The Trump administration has also ordered enhanced vetting of H-1B applicants and proposed a new visa selection process that would favour higher-skilled and better-paid workers. Earlier in August, ‌the ‌Department of Homeland Security, in a separate rule, added fees of up to $4,500 to applications to extend the stay of H-1B workers or to transfer employees based in other countries to the US.

World.title: Norway plans further development of Arctic drilling amid EU energy concerns
World.content:
EU reviewing support of a ban on new drilling in the Arctic as war impacts energy security.

Norway will continue developing its Arctic oil and gas resources despite European Union (EU) policy seeking to halt new fossil fuel projects in the region, according to a senior government official.

Development of reserves in the Barents Sea is to persist, Energy Minister Terje Aasland told Reuters news agency on Monday. While the EU currently supports a ban on new drilling in the Arctic on environmental grounds, it is reviewing the policy due to energy security concerns.

“In today’s geopolitical and security environment, and given the resource situation, I ⁠believe continued activity in the Barents Sea serves both Norwegian and European interests,” Aasland said ahead of ONS, Norway’s biannual energy conference, which began on Monday.

Europe has become dependent on Norway as its largest supplier of natural gas since Russia’s invasion of Ukraine in 2022. The Scandinavian nation meets around 30 percent of gas demand in the EU and UK.

With the United States war against Iran also tightening energy markets, such consumers are starting to rethink policy.

Norway has ⁠argued to EU officials that the parts of the Barents Sea opened to oil and gas activity are ice-free, and therefore less prone ⁠to oil spills and other environmental impact.

“We would develop these areas, and then it will be up to the EU whether they should have a moratorium on buying that gas ⁠or oil,” Aasland said.

Anders Opedal, CEO of Equinor, Norway’s biggest oil firm, said oil and liquefied natural gas (LNG) from the Barents Sea can be shipped anywhere in the world if rejected by the EU.



“The only thing that will suffer from this is European security. We have the flexibility,” Opedal told Reuters on the sidelines of the ONS conference.

Oslo’s approach is mirrored by the industry. French oil company Total will appoint a new exploration manager to examine new projects ⁠in Norway, CEO Patrick Pouyanne told Norwegian television.

Describing Norway as the natural energy supplier for Europe, he said Total hopes to expand its ‌market share, as EU countries seek resources and new maritime routes closer to home in light of global trade disruptions due to the US-Israel war on Iran.

World.title: Kidnappers release video showing hundreds abducted from Nigerian mosque
World.content:
Kidnappers have released a video of what appears to be a large group of people being held captive by armed men in a forested area in Nigeria.

The video emerged on Sunday, two days after gunmen abducted as many as 600 worshippers during Friday prayers at a mosque in Dekera village in Nigeria’s north-central Niger state.

The incident comes as Nigeria prepares for presidential elections in January, with security likely to be high on the agenda due to a wave of mass kidnappings for ransom across the north of the country.

Dekera village residents have reported that gunmen took people away in simultaneous raids on several communities.

In the video, posted on Facebook and WhatsApp and circulating widely, children can be heard crying. A gunman speaking in the Hausa language speaks directly to families of the captives, telling them to identify relatives.

“These are all your people,” the gunman ⁠says.

News agencies reported that they could not verify the exact date or location where the video was filmed. However, no older version of the video has been found posted online before Sunday.

Residents, including Abdulmutallib Muqaddas Dindi, were able to confirm the identities of some ⁠of the hostages.

“We have identified our elders, relatives, and some of us have seen their wives and children in the video,” he said.

Police and state authorities have not responded to requests for comment.

Amnesty International has urged Nigerian authorities to secure the release of the worshippers, warning of the growing threat posed by mass abductions in northern Nigeria.



State Commissioner for Information and Orientation Obed Nana told the Anadolu news agency that an operation is under way to “assess the situation, track the attackers, and facilitate the rescue of the abducted worshippers”.

Mass abductions for ransom have become common in parts of northwestern and north-central Nigeria, with armed gangs frequently raiding villages, schools and highways and holding abductees until the gangs are paid large sums of money.

Increasingly, the gunmen are targeting communities further south, beyond ‌hot spots in the north.

As he prepares for the election, President Bola Tinubu has faced growing criticism over lax security.

World.title: Trump administration announces global economic war on Iran
World.content:
NewsFeed Trump administration announces global economic war on Iran

The US says it is targeting all of Iran’s sources of revenue, including oil, as Trump’s Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announces an ‘unprecedented’ economic war, warning of severe consequences for countries who continue to trade with Tehran.

World.title: Japanese delegation seeks to soothe strained ties with China
World.content:
A cross-party delegation lands in Beijing as Tokyo tries to defrost its worst China rift in decades.

Japanese lawmakers have travelled to Beijing in a bid to soothe strained relations between the two nations.

The delegation landed in China on Monday for talks aimed at restoring communication. The mission was undertaken after Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi issued comments on Taiwan that triggered a diplomatic dispute that has begun to weigh on economic relations.

The visit will run through Thursday and marks the first such consultations with senior Chinese Communist Party officials since ties soured late last year.

Relations plunged after Takaichi suggested in November that Japan could respond militarily if China attacked Taiwan, a self-governing island that Beijing claims as its own territory.

China is highly sensitive regarding Taiwan and considers questioning of its claim on the island a red line. In response to Takaichi’s comments, it warned its citizens against travel to Japan and tightened trade restrictions, including measures that reportedly disrupted the flow of rare earth minerals to Japanese firms, adding an economic sting to the diplomatic fallout.

Among those making the trip was Gaku Hashimoto, a member of the House of Representatives and Takaichi’s ruling Liberal Democratic Party. He was joined by other lawmakers from the opposition Komeito and Centrist Reform Alliance parties.

An official from Hashimoto’s office confirmed only that he had “departed for Beijing to stay for two days”.

Before leaving Tokyo, delegation member Shinichi Isa, a spokesperson for the Centrist Reform Alliance, told reporters: “Communication has been severed in all areas, and we are beginning to see their impact in many areas. I hope we can somehow find a clue to restart a dialogue.”



Isa, a former diplomat at the Japanese embassy in China, had already sounded the alarm over the situation this month in a post on X, writing that officials had always managed to stay in contact even during past low points but now “all channels between officials and ministries have been cut off.”

He described the current state of relations as the worst since diplomatic ties were normalised in 1972.

China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs said on Friday that “some people of insight from both Japan’s ruling and opposition parties” were troubled by the state of relations and hoped to help steer them back on track while calling on Tokyo to heed those voices and act to restore normal exchanges between the two countries.

Takaichi has not retracted her comment on Taiwan and is yet to respond to the concerns.

Further exchanges are planned. Former Japanese Foreign Minister Takeshi Iwaya is expected to lead another delegation to China in late September, which is to be followed by a group of Japanese business representatives later in the year, according to the Kyodo News agency.

World.title: Trump administration announces ‘economic D-day’ sanctions on Iran
World.content:
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent says US sanctions will intensify to choke off Iran’s revenues and isolate the country.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has announced an economic pressure campaign against Iran, vowing to target Tehran’s financial interests across the world.

Bessent said on Monday that the US would target all of Iran’s sources of revenue, including oil, with the aim of preventing other countries and companies from doing business with Tehran.

“Around the globe, our objective is to sever every economic lifeline that sustains this tyrannical regime until Tehran stands alone,” he said.

He said countries around the world must choose between the US and Iran, stressing that the new campaign exposes Tehran’s trade partners to secondary penalties.

Bessent emphasised that “no one is above the reach of US sanctions”.

If countries and entities “facilitate transactions and are part of the ecosystem that turns Iranian oil into money, into repression, they will be targeted”, he said.

While the US did announce a new wave of sanctions against Iran, Monday’s campaign did not target any major international economic institution for dealing with the country.

Bessent framed the push as a strong warning for countries and companies across the world.

The campaign is dubbed “Operation Economic Outcast”. Bessent also called it “economic D-day”, likening it to the Allies’ forces landing on French shores to push back against Nazi Germany during World War II.

Asked why the US is threatening Iran’s business partners instead of penalising them, Bessent said: “Well, we are giving everyone the opportunity to remedy bad behavior. Why would I want to blow up the global financial system?”



His response underscores the risk that secondary US sanctions pose to the broader international economy.

The economic pressure campaign comes nearly six months into the war with Iran, after the US and Israel launched strikes against the country without direct provocation.

While US and Israeli attacks have killed Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei and several other top officials, they have failed to dislodge the governing system in Tehran.

Tehran has responded to the US and Israeli strikes with missile and drone attacks across the region. It has also largely shut down and asserted control over the Strait of Hormuz, a major artery for global energy, sending oil and gas prices soaring.

Multiple rounds of fighting and diplomacy have failed to resolve the crisis.

Monday’s sanctions push is the latest effort by the US to pressure Iran to make major concessions, including giving up its nuclear programme and ceasing attacks on vessels in Hormuz.

In April, the US announced a blockade on Iranian ports, but Iran has remained defiant despite the naval siege.

“The blockade has clearly hurt Iran, especially its oil exports, but it hasn’t produced the political outcome Washington wants. Iran hasn’t capitulated,” Sina Toossi, a fellow at the Center for International Policy, told Al Jazeera.

“Hormuz remains heavily disrupted, and the costs to the US and global economy are mounting. So, ‘economic D-Day’ looks like an effort to intensify the pressure now that the military campaign has failed to deliver a decisive outcome.”

Bessent said US President Donald Trump has been making calls to world leaders “with specific requests to cease their interaction with the regime”.

“Those who stand with the United States will reap the rewards of our partnership. Those who tether themselves to the Iranian regime should expect to share in the isolation,” he said.

The US officials said new sanctions will target “five of Iran’s most vital lifelines”: digital assets, technology, gold, aviation and shipping.

The US Treasury also imposed fresh sanctions on 60 entities, vessels and individuals across the world – including in the United Arab Emirates, Hong Kong, China, Singapore and Switzerland – accusing them of enabling the “Iranian regime’s recklessness”.

On Sunday, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi dismissed US pressure, stressing that economic sanctions against Iran are nothing new.

“They cannot think of any other solution in confronting the great Iranian people, so they repeatedly put forward the same old plans,” Araghchi said.

World.title: Nearly one in two Ebola patients dying in DR Congo outbreak
World.content:
Nearly one in two Ebola patients dying in DR Congo outbreak

NewsFeed Nearly one in two Ebola patients dying in DR Congo outbreak

Almost one in two people infected with Ebola are dying, Democratic Republic of the Congo government figures show. The outbreak is now the deadliest in the country’s history.

World.title: Russia to seize poorly protected infrastructure as Ukraine barrage persists
World.content:
Operators could lose control of facilities if regulators find them too slow to repair damage as Ukraine attacks spur economic and societal difficulties.

President Vladimir Putin has signed a decree opening the way for the Russian state to take temporary control of critical infrastructure found to be inadequately protected from attack.

The decree, published on Monday, would allow Moscow to strip owners of physical and financial control over facilities should it be determined that they are failing to secure them or repair damage quickly. The move comes as Ukraine maintains an intense drone campaign against Russian infrastructure.

Under the decree, ownership powers would transfer to Russia’s Federal Agency for State Property Management or another designated body, which would take responsibility for the site’s safety and could conduct an inventory of its assets.

Fuel and energy facilities, including nuclear power, are included under the legislation as well as industry, communications, transport and logistics, public utilities and other facilities deemed essential to state security and economic stability.

Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, but with the front line in eastern Ukraine bogged down, the conflict has become increasingly focused on drone and missile strikes.

Kyiv has found significant success in long-range drone attacks. Its targeting of Russia’s energy infrastructure in particular has produced results, sparking fuel shortages across the country and impacting public opinion and an economy that has been enduring increased international sanctions for close to five years.

Kyiv has also struck at least two dozen warehouses belonging to Wildberries, Russia’s largest online retailer, destroying a significant share of its storage capacity and causing billions of dollars of damage to companies across the nation.



Ozon, Russia’s second largest online retailer, said on Monday that four of its logistics hubs in southern Russia had been hit.

The same day, Russia was also forced to halt operations at the Perm oil refinery, industry sources told the Reuters news agency. The facility, a major processing plant, has been hit numerous times by Ukrainian drones in recent months.

An attack last week damaged key processing units. Repairs are expected to take up to two weeks, adding to fuel shortages reported in several regions.

World.title: Iran faces 'greatest financial offensive ever', says US treasury secretary
World.content:
The US announced a host of sanctions against Iran and threatened its supporters in what Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said was "the single greatest financial offensive ever".

Labelling it an "economic D-Day" for Iran, Bessent said the US would sever all economic ties with the country and added that any nation financially partnering with Iran would also be isolated.

However, the latest threat to the Iranian regime follows several U-turns and extended deadlines from the White House in its efforts to end the conflict.

The war has led to hikes in global oil prices, and in response to the latest threat Iran warned it would shut down all oil exports from the region if the war continued.

The Iranian regime has also issued a fresh warning to shipping to not pass through the Strait of Hormuz without its permission, according to Reuters.

One fifth of the world's oil and gas usually passes through strait, a narrow waterway south of Iran, but the flow has been effectively blocked by the country since the conflict began at the end of February, leading to higher oil prices globally.

At a press conference on Monday outlining what has been called "Operation Economic Outcast", Bessent said the US was launching an "economic onslaught against Iran's financial connections around the globe".

"Iran now faces a very clear choice with only two paths before them: complete global isolation....or a path back to normalcy with an opportunity to rejoin the global economy," he said.

The treasury secretary claimed America was "no longer managing the Iranian threat, we are ending it".

Bessent said the Treasury Department had mapped networks, facilitators and financial channels used by Iran to evade sanctions to trade oil.

The department said it has issued determinations against five sectors: digital assets, technology, gold, aviation and shipping. The Treasury has also imposed sanctions on almost 60 entities, individuals and vessels.

Bessent said that such actions would "tighten the noose and block every potential source of revenue" for Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps and the wider Iranian regime.

In a warning to governments and entities assisting or trading with Iran, he said they could not "claim they are blind to enabling this activity".

He declined to highlight specific countries, but said Trump would be phoning world leaders "with specific request to cease their interactions with the regime."

While he said it was important to give people time to understand the new sanctions, he added: "they should know that that will move very quickly and that we are serious."

World.title: UK PM Burnham vows support for Ukraine despite 'outrageous threats' from Russia
World.content:
Burnham said allies were doing "everything we can" to "dig into our own stocks and help others dig into their stocks" of air defences to protect Ukraine.

"This is the moment to keep up the pressure on Russia, the moment to squeeze their ability to fund this illegal war," Burnham said, praising the "strength" of the Ukrainian people.

"Ukraine has been Europe's protector, not a drain on our security but the front line in keeping Europe safe."

It comes after Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov criticised the UK's decision to share the missile blueprints. Peskov said it prevented "even the slightest progress" towards achieving peace.

He told reporters on Monday that the Russian military was already gathering data to locate any missile production sites to destroy them.

"Britain is involved in this war on the side of the Kyiv regime. Britain methodically and regularly adds fuel to the fire," he added.

In response, Burnham said: "Who started the fire? That's the question, isn't it?"

He said the issue of missile interceptors would be the main topic at the coalition of the willing meeting.

World.title: Russia's second-biggest online retailer targeted in Ukrainian strikes
World.content:
Meanwhile, Ozon workers in Adygeysk, in the Adygea region, and Nevinnomyssk, in the Stavropol region, have been evacuated.

Videos posted on social media of the Ozon attacks have been verified by the BBC. One shows a drone hitting a warehouse in the Orenburg region, while another shows a large plume of smoke and flames rising from its warehouse in Dagestan.

Shares in Ozon fell by as much as 12% on the Moscow Exchange on Monday morning, while shares in its major shareholder, private equity firm AFK Sistema, fell by almost 13%.

When asked on Monday whether the Russian government would provide state support to Ozon, the Kremlin said it was "working with business representatives to develop various options for providing support in this difficult situation".

The overnight strikes comes a day after Ozon's site in the Samara region was hit. The company said a number of its workers had been injured.

Following that strike, Ukraine's defence ministry said on Saturday: "Systematic strikes on dual-use goods storage centres complicate the enemy's logistics and negatively affect the Russian economy as a whole.

"After Ukrainian units hit 15 of the largest logistics hubs of Wildberries, it was Ozon's turn."

Meanwhile, in Ukraine's Odesa region, overnight strikes targeted food storage facilities and energy infrastructure leading to five people being injured, the region's head Oleg Kiper said on Telegram.

Founded in 1998, Ozon is one of Russia's first online retailers. The company is second only to Wildberries in terms of scale and presence, with its pick-up posts and delivery boxes stationed across the country.

Both the Ozon and Wildberries logos are often seen together in Russia at shared pick-up points.

The targeting of these online retailers has had the effect of bringing the war closer to ordinary Russians.

Both companies have been described as "Russia's Amazon" and it is estimated that they are used by 85-90% of Russia's economically active population.

In many remote places lacking accessible shops, Russians depend on them for much of their clothes and household appliances.

But unlike Amazon, which sells goods directly alongside its marketplace business, Wildberries and Ozon act almost entirely as marketplaces, connecting independent sellers with buyers across Russia, storing and delivering their goods and handling payments.

This means many of the losses incurred in the attacks have been borne by those businesses.

The Kremlin has denied that online platforms are used for army supplies.

World.title: Israel warns of 'forceful' response to kites flown from Gaza
World.content:
Four kites were found in Kibbutz Nahal Oz, which is about 800m (2,620ft) from the Gaza border, on Friday and Saturday. Several more were found elsewhere in southern Israel last week, according to local media.

The Israeli reports cited military sources as saying they believed Hamas was behind the kites and that they might have been intended to test Israel's response.

No suspicious materials were attached to the kites and they did not pose a threat, the military said.

But Katz warned there would be "zero tolerance" and said: "A balloon is treated like a kite, and a kite is treated like a drone, with or without explosives."

Residents of Nahal Oz said in a statement that they feared the return of incendiary kites and balloons, adding: "We will not accept a policy of containment when it comes to our security."

Hamas warned of "the danger of the allegations and threats" from Israel and said the kites were "basically children's toys from displacement camps".

"These threats are based on fabricated pretexts and are an attempt to justify the continuation of the aggression and violations against our people," a spokesman for the group added.

On Sunday, Palestinian health officials said two people were killed and seven others injured in two Israeli strikes in Nuseirat refugee camp and the town of al-Zawayda, both in central Gaza.

A four-year-old boy called Mohammed Taha was killed when a building in al-Zawayda, just north of Maghazi refugee camp, was bombed, according to local media.

The Israeli military said it killed the commander of a Hamas weapons manufacturing site in the Maghazi area, whom it identified as Ismail Abu Ful, and that it had warned the residents to evacuate beforehand.

"There is no ceasefire, there is nothing," Abu Ahmed, a displaced man who had been sheltering nearby, told Reuters news agency. "We want solutions, we want to live in peace."

On Monday, Palestinian media reported that a man called Mohammed Abu Asad was killed in an overnight Israeli strike on a tent in the central town of Deir al-Balah.

The Israeli military said Abu Asad was a member of the elite Nukhba forces of Hamas's military wing who had taken part in the Hamas-led 7 October 2023 attack on southern Israel.

The Israeli military launched a campaign in Gaza in response to the cross-border assault, during which about 1,200 people were killed and 251 were taken hostage.

More than 74,420 people have been killed in Israeli attacks in Gaza since then, including 1,288 since the ceasefire took effect, according to the territory's Hamas-run health ministry.

World.title: King of Norway's health has worsened, palace says
World.content:
King Harald V of Norway's health has worsened, the palace has said, as he remains in hospital receiving antibiotics for a bacterial infection in his bloodstream.

The monarch has responded to treatment despite the deterioration in his condition, according to the palace, but he will remain at Oslo University Hospital, Rikshospitalet, and on leave from royal duties until further notice.

The 89-year-old, who has been on the throne since 1991, was admitted to hospital and put on sick leave a week ago.

His son, Crown Prince Haakon, 53, has been serving as regent while his father is on leave.

King Harald has been treated in recent weeks with cortisone for a rare blood condition, haemolytic anaemia. It causes the number of red blood cells in the body to be reduced, and leads to fatigue and shortness of breath.

In April 2024, Norway's royal household said that King Harald would make a "permanent reduction" to his public engagements "out of consideration for his age". That year, the king had been fitted with a pacemaker after falling ill on holiday in Malaysia.

The Norwegian royal family has already faced a challenging year in 2026.

Crown Prince Haakon's wife, Crown Princess Mette-Marit, received a lung transplant in June after she had been diagnosed with a rare form of pulmonary fibrosis in 2018.

The transplant came two days after Mette-Marit's son Marius Borg HÃ¸iby was sentenced to four years in prison after being convicted of two counts of rape. He had denied the most serious charges and his lawyers said he would appeal the sentence.

HÃ¸iby, 29, was four when his mother married Crown Prince Haakon and is not himself a royal figure.

Also earlier in the year, documents were released revealing Mette-Marit's frequent contact with the late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

She later apologised to Norway's king and queen for her three-year friendship with Epstein and admitted to "poor judgement", adding in a national TV interview that she wished she had never met him.

World.title: Outrage in Nepal over rape and murder of three-year-old girl
World.content:
Activists and politicians in Nepal have urged the government to enact tougher laws as the alleged rape and murder of a three-year-old girl has caused outrage across the country.

Nepal has seen continued protests since the girl was found dead last week, three days after she went missing in Madhesh province.

Nine people have been arrested in connection with the case, a local police spokesman told the BBC.

The crime has triggered demands for reform. Police have also been accused of negligence in the initial stages of the investigation after footage of a teenage suspect was leaked onto social media.

After days of demonstrations in the city of Simara, the victim's family met government ministers, and secured a written agreement over the weekend.

The government has promised to review laws on serious offences, and create a memorial in honour of the child.

The incident has also opened a wider debate over how Nepal deals with young offenders, with some campaigners pushing for harsher punishments for minors convicted of rape or murder.

Prominent human rights activist Gauri Pradhan called the attack a "very painful incident and the government should punish anyone involved in such atrocious act. There should be some serious efforts for wider reforms".

However, he cautioned against calls for the introduction of the death penalty.

There has also been anger after a video showing a teenage suspect giving a statement about the suspected murder was uploaded to social media, sparking questions as to how footage of the individual under police custody was leaked.

"We have so far found one police personnel directly involved in the [leak] and have initiated action against him," chief district officer of Bara district, Dharmendra Kumar Mishra, told the BBC.

"If more officers are found, they will also be punished. We have zero tolerance against such practice."

More than 25,500 accusations of rape and sexual abuse were filed between July 2017 to July 2025, according to Nepalese Police.

Of these cases, more than 3,200 female victims were under the age of 10, the police say.

World.title: Nearly three million Teslas recalled in China over hidden door handles
World.content:
Minimalistic door handles became a signature feature of electric vehicles (EVs), but the controversial designs are now at the centre of China's biggest car recall, affecting more than 4 million vehicles.

The recall, which includes 2.98 million Chinese-made Teslas, follows safety concerns that the hidden door handles are difficult to locate and open in emergency situations.

Other brands affected by the recall include Chinese carmakers XPeng, Xiaomi and Geely.

The recalled vehicles will have a warning label stuck on the interior door and receive a software update to automatically lower the windows in a crash.

The designs have come under scrutiny after two fatal crashes in China involving Xiaomi EVs, in which power failures were suspected to have prevented doors from being opened.

Tesla said in a statement on Friday that it was recalling some of its Model 3, Y, S and X vehicles due to door handles that are "difficult to identify and operate because their colour is similar to the interior trim".

"In extreme situations such as a severe collision causing the vehicle's low-voltage system to fail, this could hinder occupants from quickly opening the doors to escape and impede rescue efforts by those outside the vehicle, posing a safety hazard," it said.

Tesla said it would place warning labels on the recalled vehicles and issue a software update to automatically lower a vehicle's windows after a collision.

It is not clear if the affected firms plan to make a similar recall for the rest of the world.

The BBC has contacted Tesla, XPeng, Xiaomi and Geely for comment.

The use of hidden handle designs has "snowballed" after Chinese brands were quick to copy the "sleek" look of Tesla's Model S sedan since 2014, said Tu Le, the founder of consultancy Sino Auto Insights.

The use of warning labels and a software update is more of a "band-aid" than a lasting solution for the issue, he added.

In February, Chinese authorities announced a ban on hidden door handles.

Under new rules due to take effect on 1 January 2027, cars will only be allowed to be sold in China if they have a mechanical release on both the inside and outside of their doors.

Tesla's door handles were also involved in a probe by US safety regulators after reports that they suddenly stopped working, leaving children trapped in the cars.

In July, the US National Highway Traffic Safety Administration suggested creating a new formal safety standard for all carmakers.

The BBC has contacted the agency for comment.

World.title: Sonya Massey's killer Sean Grayson dies in US prison
World.content:
Sean Grayson, the white US police officer convicted of murdering a black woman, Sonya Massey, during an incident at her home in 2024, has died in prison at age 32.

Grayson shot dead Massey, 36, during an exchange that took place after she reported a suspected intruder at her residence in Illinois. The killing reignited the debate about police brutality in the US.

Grayson said he fired because he thought Massey was about to throw a pot of boiling water on him. He was last year found guilty of second-degree murder.

The former police officer was undergoing treatment for colon cancer. His lawyer Daniel Fultz confirmed to the BBC that Grayson had died on Sunday, but did not disclose the cause.

The BBC has asked the Illinois Department of Corrections for comment.

Lawyers for Massey's family said: "Grayson's death in custody from cancer does not bring Sonya back."

"We wish his family prayers of peace, as we do for all who grieve a loved one. Sonya's family knows that pain all too well and will grieve her loss the rest of their days," the lawyers said, according to CBS News, the BBC's US partner.

Protests took place across the US in the aftermath of Massey's death, and then-President Joe Biden declared that the late woman "should be alive today".

World.title: Otedola buys 95.7 million First HoldCo shares, moves stake up 27.7%
World.content:
Femi Otedola, the chairman of First HoldCo Plc, acquired 95.7 million new shares in the banking group, taking his stake in the company to 27.70 per cent.

In a regulatory filing signed by the group’s Company Secretary, Abiola Baruwa, on Monday, Mr Otedola purchased 95,699,240 additional shares at N131.48 per share, valued at N12.58 billion.

The additional share purchase represents 0.21 per cent of the company’s outstanding shares and was made through Calvados Global Services Limited.

After the purchase, Mr Otedola now holds about 12.14 billion shares in the financial institution, representing 27.70 per cent of the company’s outstanding shares.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Based on the financial institution’s opening price of N129.95 on Monday at the Nigerian Exchange Limited (NGX), the First HoldCo chair’s total shareholding in the company is valued at about N1.58 trillion.

The new share acquisition is another purchase by Mr Otedola in recent times, as the businessman has been increasing his investment in the financial institution.

In recent weeks, the tycoon has cumulatively purchased over 2.16 billion shares of the lender. The latest share purchase is the third time in August that Mr Otedola has increased his stake in the financial services group, following his acquisitions of 147.7 million and 138 million shares on 17 August and 7 August, respectively.

Also, on 30 July, Mr Otedola increased his stake in the financial services group by acquiring an additional 1.78 billion shares at N124.90 per share, valued at about N222.2 billion.

The steady accumulation of shares has further strengthened Mr Otedola’s position as First HoldCo’s largest shareholder, overtaking RC Investment, the bridge holder that previously held the largest stake in the company at about 22.94 per cent.

RC Investment emerged in July 2025 as the trustee for 10.4 billion shares simultaneously offloaded by Oba Otudeko and Oye Hassan-Odukale, who were among First HoldCo’s major shareholders at the time, in a single-day transaction.

World.title: Osun constitutes committee to disburse N500m fund to election violence victims
World.content:
The Osun State Government has constituted a 10-member committee to verify victims of election-related violence and oversee the disbursement of the N500 million endowment fund promised by Governor Ademola Adeleke after his re-election victory.

The committee, announced on Monday, is expected to receive and verify petitions, claims and supporting evidence from people affected by the violence and recommend appropriate relief for those found eligible.

The development comes barely a week after Mr Adeleke announced the fund following his victory in the 15 August governorship election, during which he acknowledged that the political contest had come at a heavy human cost, including deaths, injuries, destruction of property and disrupted livelihoods.

The governor had said the intervention was intended to support verified victims and their families and promised that beneficiaries would not be discriminated against on the basis of political affiliation, religion, ethnicity, gender or social status.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Following the 15 August governorship election, the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) declared Mr Adeleke winner after securing 511,067 votes to defeat the All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate, Bola Oyebamiji, who polled 444,815 votes.

The newly constituted committee is chaired by the Speaker of the Osun State House of Assembly, Adewale Olumide, while Sola Sonibare, Executive Secretary of the Osun Investment Promotion Agency, will serve as secretary.

Its membership is comprised of representatives of civil society organisations, the Nigeria Police Force, Department of State Services, Ministries of Information and Justice, as well as other government officials.

According to the government’s statement, the committee is expected to ensure that the fund is administered transparently, fairly and strictly for verified victims.

“The committee is mandated to receive and verify petitions, claims and supporting evidence submitted by victims; determine the eligibility of claimants; and recommend appropriate relief to verified victims in accordance with the guidelines approved by the State Government,” the statement read.

Response to Osun’s election violence?

The establishment of the committee is the latest government response to a wave of violence that surrounded the state’s governorship election.

PREMIUM TIMES reported how violence claimed the lives of several people and left others injured, with political parties repeatedly trading accusations over responsibility for attacks.

Among the victims remembered by the governor was 14-year-old Ezekiel Olapade, who was shot dead in Ilobu, Irepodun Local Government Area, in June. His death drew fresh concerns over politically linked violence in the state ahead of the election.

Other victims named include Aderogba Ajayi, Remi Abass and Kolade Eluyera, alongside what he described as “many other victims whose lives were cut short or permanently affected by electoral violence.”

Mr Eluyera was killed in Ikire in May, with the police confirming that he was shot dead. The incident triggered accusations and counter-accusations between the Accord Party and the APC, although neither party was established as responsible for the killing.

The violence became significant enough for civil society organisations and other stakeholders to raise concerns about the safety of voters ahead of the election.

A report by Kimpact Development Initiative, for instance, identified 73 election-related violent incidents resulting in 29 deaths in the build-up to the election and listed 12 local government areas as high-risk. Amnesty International also warned of escalating violence and reported concerns around Osogbo, Ede, Ife, Oriade, Ijebu-Ijesha, Ilobu and Ikire.

Violence persists after election

The violence surrounding Osun’s governorship election did not end with the declaration of Mr Adeleke as winner. In the days after the poll, fresh confrontations erupted in different parts of the state as rival political groups battled over control of local government secretariats and transportation unions.

On 17 August, two days after the election, gunshots rang out at the Ilesa East Local Government Secretariat as supporters of the Accord Party attempted to overtake the secretariat following the party’s victory.

Similar tension was reported at other council secretariats as the political transition triggered renewed attempts by competing factions to assert control.

The developments were significant because the disputes over Osun’s local governments had already persisted before the governorship election, with rival parties laying competing claims to the councils.

The post-election tensions later spilled into the transport sector. On 24 August, a confrontation broke out at the Naira and Kobo Garage in Ikire, Irewole Local Government Area, amid competing claims over control of the motor park. In the clash, five people were reportedly killed.

The police confirmed to PREMIUM TIMES that there was shooting at the location but said they were still gathering information before confirming reports of casualties.

World.title: Sanwo-Olu, Lai Mohammed, Gbenga Daniel to discuss 2027 elections, insecurity at 7th Freedom Online lecture
World.content:
Challenges facing the economy and insecurity, especially associated with elections in a developing economy like Nigeria, will be the focus of discussion at the seventh yearly lecture of Freedom Online (www.freedomonline.com.ng) on 3 September in Lagos.

Freedom Online, according to a statement by its Managing Director/Editor-in-Chief, Gabriel Akinadewo, is focusing on how to tackle insecurity during the lecture “because it has become a monster, threatening to consume the nation-state called Nigeria.”

“What does the future hold for Nigeria after the 2027 general elections? How will the election be conducted in a way that will be acceptable to all? Will the outcome lay a solid foundation for the future of the country?

“We believe that actions of politicians, security agents and INEC officials, before, during and after the election will, one way or the other, decide the fate of the more than 200 million Nigerians in this geographical space. Obviously, insecurity, part of which is thuggery during elections, leads to poverty, underdevelopment and other social vices. Nigeria’s political, economic and social fabric is disintegrating because of this time bomb and the outcome of the election will go a long way to decide Nigeria’s future in global affairs.”

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Akinadewo said Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu of Lagos State is the Special Guest Speaker while former Information & Culture Minister, Lai Mohammed and former Ogun State Governor, Gbenga Daniel, are the Chairman and Special Guest of Honour respectively.

The President of the Nigerian Guild of Editors (NGE) and Editor of Vanguard, Eze Anaba, is the Chief Host.

World.title: UPDATED: Ogogo buried in Ilaro
World.content:
Veteran actor and screenwriter Taiwo “Ogogo” Hassan was buried at his residence in Ilaro, Ogun State, shortly after a special prayer for him at the Asade Agunloye Pavilion.

Kira, one of Ogogo’s daughters, confirmed on her Instagram page that the actor was buried on Monday in accordance with Islamic rites. “God, they’ve buried my daddy,” she wrote.

Several of Ogogo’s colleagues, friends and associates attended the burial to pay their final respects. They included Madam Saje, Dele Odule, Yinka Quadri, Jide Kosoko, Femi Adebayo, Toyosi Adesanya, Ireti Osayemi, Sunny Alli, and Muyideen “Lala” Oladapo.

Others included Owolabi Ajasa, Saidi Balogun, Fathia Balogun, Kola Ajeyemi, Sanusi Izihaq, and Kudirat Abeniade.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The mourners struggled to contain their emotions as they accompanied Ogogo’s remains to his final resting place, with several of his colleagues breaking down in tears.

Before the burial, Ogogo’s colleagues, friends and associates paid tribute to him, recalling his kindness and describing him as a man who brought joy to those around him and lived a meaningful life.

His close friend, Quadri, was particularly emotional, as he was seen crying uncontrollably before and after Ogogo’s burial.

Backstory

PREMIUM TIMES earlier reported that the actor died on Sunday after battling stage-four cancer. His remains arrived in his hometown, Ilaro, late on Sunday, drawing mourners who gathered to honour the late film icon and console his family.

Ogogo’s death followed an appeal by his daughters, Kira and Haleemah, who revealed that he was diagnosed with cancer and urged Nigerians to help the family explore possible treatment options, including traditional medicine, after alleging that a hospital had refused to treat him.

The sisters clarified that they were not seeking financial donations. Their appeal, however, prompted members of the public to offer assistance, including recommendations for hospitals and traditionalist homes where the actor could receive treatment.

As Ogogo battled for his life, his colleagues rallied around him, sought medical assistance and organised a prayer session where they asked God to intervene and restore his health.

Ogogo began his acting career in 1981 while working as a mechanic. He later left his job with the water corporation in 1994 to pursue acting as a full-time career.

Before his death, Ogogo appeared in numerous films, including “Atitebi”, “Agbelebu”, “Agbo-Odaju”, “Danfo Driver”, “Owo Blow”, “Amerah”, “Aníkúlápó”, “Bank Alert”, “IGE”, and “Aníkúlápó: Rise of the Spectre”, among others.

World.title: Woman who died at Umahi’s residence buried amid autopsy dispute
World.content:
Mary Habila, a nurse who died under controversial circumstances at the Ebonyi State residence of the Minister of Works, David Umahi, has been buried by her family, despite a dispute over an autopsy.

PREMIUM TIMES earlier reported that Habila, who was attached to Umahi, was brought in dead to the David Umahi Federal University Teaching Hospital, Uburu, Ebonyi State, on 27 June.

Burial in Kaduna

PREMIUM TIMES gathered that her remains were buried at her home town in Nok, Jaba Local Government Area of Kaduna State, on Friday, 21 August.

Several photographs circulating on Facebook showed her family members and members of her church, Evangelical Church Winning All, performing the burial rites.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Her tomb was tiled with an upright memorial headstone at the back bearing the inscription: “In Loving Memory of Late Miss Mary Habila (Mara).”

Controversial death, autopsy dispute

Habila’s burial occurred weeks after a dispute over the autopsy and public outrage concerning the controversies surrounding her death.

Her death at the minister’s residence on 27 June only became public in July – about two weeks later – which triggered concerns and outrage.

Many Nigerians called for Umahi’s resignation from office following the controversy, while the minister has repeatedly denied involvement in the nurse’s death.

Following calls by many Nigerians for an autopsy to establish the cause of death, Umahi appealed to the police to conduct it.

However, the family opposed the autopsy and initially fixed the burial date for 17 July, but the police insisted on proceeding with the autopsy.

The minister further appealed to the bereaved family to reconsider their insistence on shunning the autopsy on the late nurse’s body, stressing that the post-mortem examination would help establish the actual cause of her death amid mounting allegations of foul play.

However, the family subsequently wrote to the Inspector-General of Police (IGP), Olatunji Disu, demanding the immediate release of the body for burial.

They later postponed the burial due to the controversy.

Recently, a civil society organisation, the Kwechiri Unity Forum, filed a lawsuit against the Works minister and the IGP alongside others over Habila’s death.

World.title: Peter Obi speaks on Tinubu, Atiku’s academic records at 2027 campaign flag-off
World.content:
The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has asked Nigerians to take advantage of the 2027 campaign period to examine each candidate’s academic records and proposals and ask “tough questions.”

Mr Obi, a former governor of Anambra State, spoke during a press conference on Friday to flag off his 2027 presidential campaign.

The conference was streamed live on his Facebook page and other social media platforms.

President Bola Tinubu’s birth records and academic history have been a subject of controversy before his election in 2023. The controversy resurfaced recently ahead of the 2027 elections.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Speaking at the press conference, Mr Obi, without naming any candidate, called for scrutiny of the candidates’ records and academic histories for the election.

“Every candidate must be willing to present their credentials, defend their records, and subject their vision to open scrutiny.

“No candidate should hide behind the high walls of power, send proxies or surrogates to the hustings, and expect Nigerians to entrust them with the leadership of the country,” he said.

“Every candidate seeking the presidency must have the courage to come before the people, answer their questions, defend their records, and subject their vision to public scrutiny.”

Apart from Mr Tinubu, who is a member of the ruling All Progressives Congress, Atiku Abubakar of the African Democratic Congress is among the top presidential candidates for next year’s election.

My agenda for Nigeria

Mr Obi also launched his economic and security strategies for Nigeria.

The NDC candidate vowed that if elected Nigeria’s president in 2027, he would leverage the comparative advantages of each region of the country to drive production, investment, job creation, and the sharing of prosperity.

He lamented that the country was currently battling myriad challenges, such as insecurity, economic hardship, and food insecurity, with many bearing the brunt of these realities.

“Yet I do not believe Nigeria lacks the ability to overcome these challenges. We have the people, resources, market, talent, and enterprise.

“What we must do now is turn these strengths into security, productivity, and shared prosperity,” he said.

“Nigeria’s diversity is an economic strength. Each region has distinct assets, and national policy must unlock those assets while connecting them to one productive economy.”

The former governor said the North-west of Nigeria could expand agriculture and manufacturing while strengthening education and security, with the North-east speeding up reconstruction, restoring livelihoods, and expanding agriculture, education, enterprise, and regional trade.

According to him, the North-Central can strengthen food production and processing, while the South-west can build on its strengths in manufacturing, technology, finance, trade, and the creative economy.

He said the South-east can expand its entrepreneurial and industrial strength, while the South-south can derive greater value from oil and gas while expanding maritime services, fisheries, agriculture, and other productive sectors.

“The Federal Capital Territory must demonstrate what efficient urban planning, transportation, housing, sanitation, security, and public services can achieve.

“Every region must produce. Every region must contribute. Every region must benefit,” he said.

Economic agenda

Mr Obi said that if he and his running mate, Rabiu Kwankwaso, are elected in 2027, their administration would develop an economic agenda that would put production, investment, enterprise, and human capital at the centre of their leadership.

“We will raise agricultural productivity by securing farming communities, expanding irrigation, improving rural roads and storage, and linking farmers to finance and markets.

“We will also strengthen manufacturing and agro-processing so Nigeria can export more finished goods and capture greater value from its resources.

“We will create a business environment where entrepreneurs can invest, hire, and grow without unnecessary regulatory or infrastructure barriers,” he said.

“And we will manage public finances responsibly. Every Naira should have a clear purpose, and major public investments should have measurable outcomes.”

The former governor reiterated his promise to turn Nigeria from a consumption to a production economy, saying the country’s over 200 million population, which makes it one of Africa’s largest domestic markets and labour forces, is “an opportunity we must seize to turn the future of our country around.”

Security agenda

Mr Obi noted that no nation can prosper when its people cannot live, farm, travel, or do business safely, stressing that insecurity has displaced millions of Nigerians and continues to disrupt agriculture and other economic activities.

“We must improve intelligence gathering and coordination among security agencies, strengthen policing and border management, and make better use of technology.

“We must also support lawful community-based systems that identify threats early and enable effective responses,” he said.

“Security policy must also address the conditions that make vulnerable young people susceptible to criminal recruitment.”

Health

On healthcare, Mr Obi argued that Nigeria’s health indicators remain deeply concerning despite the sector’s importance, but assured that his administration would reverse the situation.

“We will strengthen healthcare, improve maternal and child health, expand access to essential medicines, and equip healthcare workers to serve effectively,” he said.

World.title: How Anambra govt got involved in ‘fake’ federal agency – Official
World.content:
The Anambra State Government has detailed how the state government got involved with the recently uncovered fake federal agency in Nigeria.

PREMIUM TIMES reported on Friday that the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) uncovered another “fake” agency, with President Bola Tinubu suspending three top officials identified as enablers and ordering the arrest of the frontrunner, George Nwabueze.

The phoney agency, known as the National Brands Development and Made in Nigeria Special Project Office, was said to be operating within the Office of the Secretary to the Government of the Federation.

The suspected permanent secretaries are M.S. Danjuma, Nadungu Gagare, and Richard P. Pheelangwah.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

However, Mr Nwabueze, who describes himself as the National Coordinator and Executive Director of the agency, has continued to reject the ICPC’s allegation that the organisation was operating without government authorisation.

The agency had coordinators across different states in Nigeria, including Anambra State.

How we were tricked by the fake agency

In a statement on Sunday, the Secretary to the Anambra State Government (SSG), Chiamaka Nnake, said she was appointed as the state coordinator for the fake agency after Governor Charles Soludo received a letter from the office in January requesting nomination of a focal person from the state.

“In response, the governor, in February 2026, nominated me as the State Focal Person for Anambra State.

“Following the nominations, Focal Persons from the 36 states have been in a WhatsApp group engaging on issues relating to the activities of the office,” Ms Nnake recalled.

The SSG said the same office recently wrote to the state, requesting that Anambra should host the South-east Made-in-Nigeria Fair.

“The request was approved, and an inaugural meeting was held about two weeks ago, with the National Coordinator in attendance. Since then, the State Committee has been working on preparations for the Fair, which is scheduled to take place from 2nd to 5th December 2026,” she said.

Ms Nnake denied any involvement in establishing the fake agency.

“Beyond these official interactions and engagements, I have no knowledge of, involvement in, or connection with any other activities, claims, or developments attributed to the said office.

“I therefore wish to make it clear that anything beyond the above-mentioned official interactions is entirely outside my knowledge and involvement,” she said.

The fourth discovery

This is the fourth “fake” agency to be uncovered by the ICPC in less than six weeks.

In July, the commission uncovered a fake agency known as the Presidential Foreign Investment Promotion Council (PFIPC), prompting President Tinubu’s directive to the ICPC to probe the PFIPC and submit its report within 30 days.

Earlier this month, the ICPC submitted an interim report to Mr Tinubu on its investigation into the alleged fictitious agency.

The commission announced in the report that it had uncovered two additional fake agencies established by the self-proclaimed Director-General of the organisation, Adeniyi Adeyemi.

The two additional agencies were the FCT Investment Promotion Agency and the Foreign Investment Promotion Agency.

World.title: One operative, six gunmen killed during shootout in Anambra – Police
World.content:
At least one security operative and six gunmen were killed in Anambra State during a deadly gun battle between a joint team of security operatives and a terror group in the state.

Tochukwu Ikenga, the police spokesman in Anambra State, disclosed this in a statement on Sunday.

Mr Ikenga, a superintendent of police, said the shootout occurred on Saturday at Amiyi, a community in the Ogbaru Local Government Area of Anambra.

The spokesman said the joint security team killed the six gunmen when they raided a hideout of the suspected criminals in a forest in the community.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The joint team, he said, comprised police operatives from the Rapid Response Squad in Awkuzu; personnel of the State Security Service; officials of the 302 Artillery Regiment in Onitsha; officers of the Nigerian Navy from Ogbaru; and members of the Agunaechemba Vigilante group in the community.

Mr Ikenga said, in response to a tip-off, the team trekked for about four hours through difficult terrain and dense palm forest before arriving at the suspected criminal group’s hideout.

“On sighting the security personnel, the suspects opened fire, leading to a prolonged exchange of gunfire.

“At the end of the encounter, six suspected members of the armed group were neutralised, while others fled the area, with some reportedly sustaining gunshot injuries,” he said.

The spokesman said the security operatives recovered two pump-action guns and charms and then dismantled the camps and structures believed to be associated with the group.

“The operation, however, recorded the death of one security operative and injury to another when an explosive device suspected to have been planted in the area detonated,” he said, without providing the identity of the injured and slain operatives.

“The injured operative is currently receiving medical attention in a hospital.”

Praise for the operatives

Mr Ikenga said the Commissioner of Police in Anambra State, Nnanna Ama, has commended the courage, resilience and professionalism of the joint team and vigilante operatives

Mr Ama noted that the security operatives took part in the operation despite the difficult terrain and hostile environment involved.

The commissioner described the successful operation as a further demonstration of the importance of intelligence sharing, inter-agency cooperation and community support in confronting violent criminals and disrupting their operational bases.

The police chief also commiserated with the family, colleagues and associates of the fallen security operative, while wishing the injured operative a speedy and full recovery.

He reassured residents of the state that the command, in collaboration with other security agencies, will continue to sustain intelligence-led operations aimed at dismantling criminal camps, recovering illegal arms and preventing violent groups from establishing operational footholds in the state.

“The command, therefore, urges members of the public to remain vigilant and continue to provide timely and credible information to security agencies, as community cooperation remains critical to sustaining the peace and security of the state,” he said.
