World.title: Iraq, Qatar provide oil for loading inside Hormuz via bids
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Trade sources reported on Monday that Iraq’s national oil marketer, SOMO, and QatarEnergy are presenting crude oil through unusual bids that mandate purchasers to load cargoes within the Strait of Hormuz.

SOMO announced that it is offering Basrah Medium and Basrah Heavy crude for loading in September from either the Basrah oil port or a single point mooring, along with the necessary supporting facilities, as reported by Reuters.

QatarEnergy provided free-on-board oil loading at al-Shaheen, Qatar Marine, and Qatar Land ports in September and October.

Earlier, SOMO provided substantial discounts on Basrah crude in August to entice customers to load shipments from the Strait of Hormuz.

SOMO asked potential term purchasers to designate contractual volumes of Basrah Medium or Basrah Heavy crude for complimentary onboard delivery from the Basrah Oil Terminal or other port-related infrastructure.

Iraq’s oil marketer provided discounts ranging between $25 and $27 per barrel on Basrah Medium, according to the loading period. It provided discounts of $27.80 to $29.80 a barrel for Basrah Heavy.

Maritime traffic in the Strait of Hormuz decreased due to ongoing military operations in the region and heightened shipping security risks.

The significant price reduction aims to compensate for rising maritime insurance costs and freight expenses by transferring transit risk to purchasers.

World.title: Iraq to introduce new banknotes with three zeros removed
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq intends to remove three zeros from its currency to modernize financial transactions, reduce physical cash circulation, and return stockpiled funds to the official banking system.

Under the suggestion, a 25,000-Iraqi dinar note would become 25 Iraqi dinars, but the currency’s purchasing power and true financial value would stay unaffected.

According to Jamal Kocher, a Kurdish member of the Iraqi parliament’s finance committee, Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi has asked for the removal of zeros from invoices.

Kocher told The New Region that if the plan is implemented, 1,000 Iraqi dinars would be converted to one dinar, while 25,000 dinars would be equivalent to 25 dinars.

Earlier in August, Communications Minister Mustafa Sanad acknowledged the plan to eliminate the zeros and modify the currency.

The redenomination strategy aims to bring undeclared cash, estimated to be between 8 and 10 trillion Iraqi dinars that are currently held outside banks, back into official channels. This initiative seeks to combat crime, corruption, and money laundering.

According to the idea, everyday prices, incomes, and savings will alter correspondingly, resulting in a direct mathematical shift rather than a change in actual wealth.

Iraq has sought printing partners in the United Kingdom and Australia, as well as its traditional suppliers in France and Germany, to create an estimated 7.5 billion new banknotes.

While government officials such as the Communications Minister and Finance Committee members have emphasized the importance of an official implementation date, the Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) has yet to present a formal draft bill to parliament.

World.title: Iraq to raise oil exports via Turkey’s Ceyhan to 750,000 bpd
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Oil announced on Sunday a proposal to increase oil exports through the Turkish port of Ceyhan to 750,000 barrels per day by using tanker trucks to transport crude oil from southern oilfields.

The spokesperson for the Iraqi Oil Ministry, Salim al-Rikabi, told the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA) that the plan includes increasing exports through southern ports.

Iraq and Turkey recently inked a one-year short-term deal to continue operations through the critical Iraq-Turkey oil pipeline.

The agreement, reached in Ankara following discussions between Turkish Energy Minister Alparslan Bayraktar and Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair, guarantees the ongoing transportation of at least 750,000 barrels of Iraqi crude oil per day to the Turkish port of Ceyhan.

Turkey’s state-owned crude oil and natural gas pipeline corporation (BOTAS) signed an agreement with Iraq’s State Organization for Marketing of Oil (SOMO) and the North Oil Company (NOC).

The new deal is now valid for 12 months until both countries develop a new, long-term legislative framework.

The previous agreement, which was reached in 1973, officially expired on July 27.

The short extension of the deal is crucial for Iraq’s revenue from oil exports, as Baghdad seeks alternative export routes to mitigate risks linked to the Strait of Hormuz.

World.title: Eto’o urges support for embattled FIFA president Infantino
World.content:
Paris – Former Cameroon star Samuel Eto’o has thrown his support behind beleaguered FIFA president Gianni Infantino, saying he “hasn’t done anything wrong” despite facing mounting pressure to step down over a controversial World Cup sell-off plan.

Infantino has come under intense scrutiny since the collapse of a proposal to secure private investment in FIFA tournaments, including the World Cup.

UEFA, which oversees European football, has threatened a boycott of FIFA competitions with several continental and national federations also withdrawing their support for Infantino.

However, Eto’o, president of the Cameroonian football federation, dismissed criticism of Infantino’s leadership, suggesting the backlash was driven largely by political manoeuvring ahead of FIFA’s presidential election next year.

“I don’t think that President Gianni Infantino has done anything wrong,” the former Barcelona, Inter Milan and Chelsea striker told CNN.

“I think the timing of all of that is because there’s an election coming out.”

Infantino’s plan, which would reportedly have distributed substantial funding to FIFA’s 211 member associations, faced strong opposition from several confederations and was ultimately abandoned.

The FIFA president remains under pressure, with the possibility of a no-confidence vote being triggered. UEFA, the Asian Football Confederation and CONCACAF — which governs North and Central America and the Caribbean — have all voiced concerns over FIFA’s direction in recent weeks.

But the Confederation of African Football (CAF) earlier this month “unanimously reconfirmed its support” for Infantino, and Eto’o’s backing is aligned with that position.

“President Gianni Infantino has changed football,” said Eto’o, urging fellow African countries to support the Swiss official.

“He’s given opportunities to nations that didn’t have those opportunities to take part in the most beautiful tournament, the World Cup. He enabled smaller nations to get seats at these competitions.

“He has helped our continent. He’s helped our federations to develop much more quickly, and we need to acknowledge that. We need to accept and recognise what he’s done, and we should support him for everything he’s done up to now.”

World.title: Trump claims Iran ‘collapsing’ as US threatens ‘economic D-Day’
World.content:
Washington – US President Donald Trump said Monday that Iran was “collapsing” as Washington prepared to announce the details of a new economic pressure campaign that Tehran has derided as an admission of defeat.

Almost six months into their war, the two sides are locked in a stalemate, with peace talks stalled, Iran keeping the key Strait of Hormuz shut and Washington persisting with a naval counter-blockade of Iran.

Under political pressure at home over the economic impacts of the conflict, Trump has pivoted away from military action to economic levers.

“IRAN IS COMPLETELY COLLAPSING!!!” the president posted Monday in his trademark all-caps style on his social media platform Truth Social.

His remarks came hours after US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, in a column for the Financial Times, declared that an “economic D-Day” had begun against Tehran and warned that any country that continued to enable the Islamic republic would become a “global pariah”.

Bessent also claimed on X that the US had “dismantled Iran’s military capabilities, destroyed nearly 100 percent of its military factories, and buried its nuclear programme”.

Iran responded with defiance, saying the latest US measures were an admission of military defeat, and it warned countries against aiding Washington.

Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi posted on X that the US turn to financial warfare proved Bessent’s claims false.

“Your narrative doesn’t add up,” Gharibabadi said, asking why, if Washington had achieved its goals, “there is a need for ‘the largest financial invasion in history’ and the mobilisation of ‘all institutions and powers’ of the United States!

“Is this a victory or an admission of America’s defeat?”

The US and Israel linked the launch of their war in February to Iran’s nuclear programme, but the focus since the early days of fighting has been on the Strait of Hormuz, a vital route for global oil and gas supplies.

Tehran continues to blockade the strait, which it did not restrict before the war, driving up global inflation and heaping domestic pressure on Trump ahead of mid-term elections in November.

– Oil exports plunge –

Bessent was due to set out details of the US plan on Monday, but it is unclear how much more economic pressure Washington can put on Tehran.

The US naval blockade of Iran has seen its oil exports via the Strait of Hormuz fall from two million barrels a day pre-war to just 0.4 million by mid-August, according to maritime tracker Kpler.

Meanwhile, the country has been under crushing international sanctions for decades, with a brief period of easing under a 2015 nuclear deal that Trump later ripped up as part of a “maximum pressure” campaign.

The Islamic republic has weathered those efforts and, before the war, continued to export millions of barrels of oil, mostly to China, and evade sanctions through complex international financial networks.

Bessent and Trump have both warned countries against helping Iran, signalling a shift in their focus, with the Treasury secretary’s FT column dwelling on nations who “appease” and “enable” Iran.

Tehran responded on Monday by warning countries not to cooperate with the US efforts. Foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei said taking part would “definitely have its own consequences”.

For ordinary Iranians, the standoff is likely to bring only more economic pain after years of rampant inflation, which in December and January fuelled massive anti-government protests.

Sarah Hassanbeigi, a 32-year-old pharmacist in Tehran, put it simply: “It’s really very difficult. I don’t think people can really take this much longer.”

On Sunday, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian admitted that Iran faced “many problems in society”.

“We are striving with all our hearts to overcome inflation, livelihood problems, unemployment, and to secure the future of the people, so that they can live with dignity and pride,” Pezeshkian said.

– Delegation from Pakistan –

Last week, the Iranian president, considered a relative moderate, said Tehran should “bring the war to an end now as we are in a position of power and dignity”.

That followed supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei appointing hardliners to key security positions.

Hassanbeigi said she wanted peace. “Naturally, negotiations mean that both sides have to compromise. My personal opinion is that Iran should compromise now,” she told AFP.

Throughout the war, diplomatic efforts, pushed on by mediators, have sought a negotiated end to the conflict.

On Monday, Pakistan’s army chief was expected in Iran. Islamabad was a leading mediator in talks that helped secure an April ceasefire that later fell apart.

Omani Foreign Minister Badr al-Busaidi was also due in Iran on Tuesday, as Muscat and Tehran seek a deal on regulating passage through Hormuz.

World.title: Liverpool must improve on ‘unacceptable’ season, says Van Dijk
World.content:
Liverpool – Virgil van Dijk said Liverpool “need to show a reaction” from a bitterly disappointing season that cost Arne Slot his job as manager, but called for patience with new boss Andoni Iraola.

The Reds needed a 99th-minute equaliser from the penalty spot by Dominik Szoboszlai to rescue a 2-2 draw at Newcastle on the opening weekend of the Premier League season.

Slot guided Liverpool to glory and a 20th league title in his debut campaign in 2024/25, but paid the price for finishing fifth last season when he was dismissed in May.

Many of the same flaws were in evidence in Iraola’s first outing at St James’ Park as Newcastle sliced open the Liverpool defence on the counter-attack.

But they twice came from behind to avoid a losing start to the new season.

“It’s absolutely normal in any type of profession, work, whatever you do, if you come in new and you have new plans and new ideas, then it takes a bit of time with new players,” said Van Dijk.

“It’s down to us to do it as soon as we can, as soon as possible, because we want to improve, we want to win, we want to be better. That’s what we are going to try to do.

“We need to show a reaction from last year, that we are much better than last year, because this was very unacceptable.”

Iraola has not been aided by a lack of new arrivals in the transfer market.

Despite the departure of club legend Mohamed Salah and a long-term injury to Hugo Ekitike, Liverpool have only added Spanish winger Victor Munoz in attacking areas as well as defenders Jeremy Jacquet and Ronald Araujo.

Paris Saint-Germain’s two-time Champions League winner Bradley Barcola has been linked with a move to Anfield, while two bids for Brighton winger Yankuba Minteh have reportedly been turned down.

“Everyone wants to see quality arrive regardless and I fully trust the club and the board to make the right decisions,” Van Dijk added.

“That’s the only thing I can say, so let’s see what we are going to do.”

World.title: Iraq suggests a security council involving Iran, Saudi Arabia
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq has officially suggested forming a joint security coordination council with Iran and Saudi Arabia to address what it calls a severe crisis of trust between the two regional powers.

The Security Affairs Adviser to the Prime Minister of Iraq, Qasim al-Araji, put forward the diplomatic initiative on behalf of Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s government to stabilize the region where Iraq strives to manage its own turbulent security climate.

Baghdad clearly planned the initiative to reconcile serious tensions between Riyadh and Tehran.

Tensions rose as Saudi Arabia intercepted multiple drones aimed at its oil facilities and capital. Riyadh denounced Iran-backed militias that operate from inside Iraq.

The idea comes during a very unstable period, including recent US-Saudi joint airstrikes targeting Popular Mobilization Forces’ (PMF) sites in Iraq and leading to serious criticism from Baghdad for sovereignty violations.

Baghdad is also pressuring Tehran for waivers for oil tankers from Iran’s navigation restrictions in the Strait of Hormuz.

Additionally, al-Araji underlined Iraq’s transition to ultimate domestic sovereignty.

With the scheduled withdrawal of the US-led international coalition forces from Iraq, Baghdad is adopting a strategy to put all armed factions and weaponry under strict state supervision, consolidating the country’s ultimate authority over war and peace choices.

Neither Saudi Arabia nor Iran has released a formal public response to the Iraqi initiative.

World.title: Iraq foreign reserves decline 11.6% to $86.17B in June 2026
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Official financial statements from the Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) show that Iraq’s foreign exchange reserves declined to $86.175 billion at the end of June 2026, marking a decrease of $11.257 billion (-11.6%) compared to the $97.432 billion recorded at the close of 2025.

According to reserve records published on Monday, August 24, 2026, the contraction followed an early-year peak above $102 billion before downward momentum set in through the second quarter.

Monthly Reserve Trajectory (H1 2026)

End of 2025 Baseline: $97.432 billion

January 2026: $101.082 billion

February 2026 (Peak): $102.131 billion

March 2026: $100.341 billion

April 2026: $97.809 billion

May 2026: $93.673 billion

June 2026:$86.175 billion(Month-over-month drop of $7.498 billion)

The overall drop reduced the local currency value of the total portfolio from 126.661 trillion IQD at the end of 2025 to 112.027 trillion IQD by June 30, 2026—a net decline of 14.634 trillion IQD (-11.6%).

Reserve Component End of 2025 (IQD) End of June 2026 (IQD) Net Change Change (%) Investments & Securities 93.266 Trillion 81.998 Trillion -11.268 Trillion -12.1% Monetary Gold Reserves 31.488 Trillion 29.415 Trillion -2.073 Trillion -6.6% Cash Vault Holdings 1.907 Trillion 0.614 Trillion -1.293 Trillion -67.8% Total Equivalent Value 126.661 Trillion 112.027 Trillion -14.634 Trillion -11.6%

The reserve reduction aligns with broader fiscal pressures in the first half of 2026, during which lower oil revenues widened the state budget deficit and prompted the central bank to meet elevated domestic foreign currency demand.

While liquid investment instruments fell by 11.268 trillion IQD to absorb trade financing and foreign wire settlements, cash assets held in central bank vaults rebounded moderately in June (up to 614 billion IQD from 366 billion IQD in May), even as overall foreign exchange reserves adjusted downward to $86.175 billion.

World.title: SIA reopens probe into 1998 massacre of 23 Kashmiri Pandits in Ganderbal
World.content:
SRINAGAR: J&K State Investigation Agency (SIA) has reopened the investigation into the 1998 Wandhama massacre of 23 people as part of a wider push to probe the killings of Kashmiri Pandits during the peak of militancy in the Valley.

According to sources, SIA has also started a probe into the killings of prominent Kashmiri Pandit advocate-politician Tika Lal Taploo and Justice Neelkanth Ganjoo.

On Jan 25, 1998, armed terrorists entered the homes of Kashmiri Pandit families in Wandhama village of Ganderbal district and gunned down 23 people. The case still remains unresolved, but SIA sources in said it will see âsubstantial progress soonâ.

Officials said SIA has undertaken a focused and comprehensive investigation into the decades-old cases to bring each of these to a logical conclusion in accordance with law.

âConcerted efforts are being made to uncover the circumstances and conspiracies underlying these cases, establish credible evidence, and identify those responsible strictly on the basis of substantiated evidence and witness testimony,â said an official.

Taploo, a prominent lawyer and then vice-president of J&K BJP, was shot dead near his residence in Srinagar in Sept 1989, in what among the first targeted killings of prominent Kashmiri Pandits as terrorism took roots in the Valley.





Justice Ganjoo, who had sentenced JKLF founder Maqbool Bhat to death, was shot dead on Nov 4, 1989 in Srinagar.

On Aug 12, SIA carried out searches at nine locations across J&K in connection with the killing of Kashmiri Pandit poet and writer Sarvanand Kaul Premi and his son by terrorists. Premi, 66, and his younger son Verinder were shot dead in Anantnag in south Kashmir on May 1, 1990, a day after they were abducted from their village.

She was abducted by terrorists from the SKIMS hostel on April 18, 1990, tortured and shot dead. Her bullet-riddled body was recovered the next day.

World.title: Facing heat over power tariff hike, J&K CM Omar Abdullah says he promised free electricity, not static rates
World.content:
SRINAGAR: Chief minister Omar Abdullah Monday defended the power tariff hike in Jammu & Kashmir, saying the increase was minimal and that his govt had never promised that electricity rates would not increase.

âWhen did we say that electricity rates will not increase? We said we will provide 200 units of free electricity to the poorest people, those who need it the most,â he said.

Hitting back at political parties protesting the tariff hike, Omar said there had been only a 6% increase after a gap of four years, whereas it was much higher earlier. âThose who point fingers at me should remember that they too were in power here at some point.

During their govt, electricity rates increased by more than 14%. They did not feel at that time that this was unfair,â he said. âFour years ago, electricity rates were increased by 15%, and even then, BJP remained silent.

â

âWe are not celebrating an increase in electricity rates. This was our compulsion. As our losses in the power sector reduce, we will not need to take such steps,â the CM added.

World.title: J&K CM Omar Abdullah asks police, security agencies to take poster threatening Kashmir Pandit employees seriously
World.content:
SRINAGAR: A new poster issued by the little-known United Liberation Council (ULC) threatening Kashmiri Pandits led community members working in the Kashmir Valley under the PM Package for Kashmiri Migrants and Non-Migrant Kashmiri Pandits to write to J&K chief secretary Atal Dulloo seeking enhanced security.

Chief minister Omar Abdullah described the threats as âhighly concerning.â

The poster contains the personal details of some Kashmiri Pandit employees, including addresses.

Omar, talking to reporters here, urged police and law-and-order agencies not to take the threats lightly. He said the agencies have a responsibility to provide security to Kashmiri Pandit employees and urged them to proactively investigate the source of the threats.

âIn a similar situation around two and a half years ago, some Pandit employees were targeted,â Omar said. He said security and law-and-order arrangements in J&K are under the control of the lieutenant-governor.

The police have issued any statement on the fresh threat. The chief secretary was not available for comment.

According to a letter from All PM Package Employeesâ Forum to the CS, âa fresh threat poster, purportedly issued by a terrorist outfit calling itself the United Liberation Council (ULC) on Aug 23, 2026, has surfaced on social media.





The poster reportedly contains threats directed towards migrant Kashmiri Pandit employees and â¦ details such as names, addresses and vehicle numbers of certain individuals.â

While the forum said the âauthenticity of the poster is yet to be verified by police and security agenciesâ, it added that âthe repeated circulation of such threat letters and posters, particularly those containing sensitive personal information, is a matter of grave concernâ.

The forum sought a review of security arrangements at places of posting, residential accommodation and transit routes of PM Package employees. It said govt should ensure that employees whose names, addresses or vehicle details have appeared in such threats receive immediate protection and necessary security guidance.

All Minority Employees Association president Sanjay Kaul said the Aug 23 poster was the third in 20 days.

âWe are only here for work. We take such threat letters seriously as they contain names and even numbers of vehicles of some Pandit employees,â Kaul said. âBefore 2022 we were working fearlessly, but not now. We seek a thorough probe,â he added.

In May 2022, Kashmiri Pandit migrant employee Rahul Bhat was shot dead by terrorists inside his office in central Kashmirâs Budgam district. He was recruited as a clerk under the PM Package for migrants in 2010-11.

The Manmohan Singh-led UPA govt had in 2008 introduced a rehabilitation package for Kashmiri Pandits living outside the Valley, including providing 6,000 govt jobs and creation of new posts. World.title: No alliance with SAD? BL Santosh says BJP to go solo in Punjab polls
World.content:

NEW DELHI: The Bharatiya Janata Party on Monday put speculation over an alliance with the Shiromani Akali Dal to rest, saying the saffron party will contest all 117 seats in the upcoming Punjab assembly elections.BJP national general secretary (organisation) BL Santosh said the party was fully prepared for the polls and would form the government in Punjab."Punjab is fully ready for change, and the BJP is fully prepared to make this change a reality. In the upcoming assembly elections, the BJP will contest all 117 Assembly seats in Punjab and, by securing a victory, will form its government in the state," Santosh said.The statement comes days after speculation grew over a possible BJP-SAD alliance following SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal's meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi.Former Union minister Harsimrat Kaur Badal had also hinted at the possibility of the Akali Dal joining hands with the BJP again, while expressing a cryptic wish for "agreements" that brought progress to Punjab from Delhi.Earlier, Shiromani Akali Dal leader Bikram Singh Majithia also said that people in Punjab want his party to join hands with the Bharatiya Janata Party for the upcoming polls.Majithia cited Punjab's status as a border state and the need to protect social harmony and the state's social fabric as reasons for public sentiment favouring a reunion."We should understand that the Shiromani Akali Dal and BJP have worked together. Vajpayee ji and Badal ji strengthened this alliance, and it continued during Modi ji's time," Majithia said.The SAD had parted ways with the National Democratic Alliance in September 2020 over the three farm laws, which were later repealed.Santosh began his two-day visit to Punjab to review the party's organisational functioning and strengthen coordination and preparedness at the grassroots level in the poll-bound state.His visit comes amid dissent within the BJP's state unit over a recent organisational reshuffle, with a section of leaders accusing the state leadership of sidelining the old cadre.

PM Modi and Trump held bilateral talks on June 17 at Evian-les-Bains on the sidelines of the G7 summit

NEW DELHI: India adopted a cautious approach and opted against holding a joint media interaction after Prime Minister Narendra Modi's meeting with US President Donald Trump in France in June amid concerns over the US president's "unpredictable behaviour", government sources told news agency PTI on Monday.The sources said that foreign delegations meeting Trump are often "wary about his unpredictable behaviour as may be seen from his interactions with the presidents of South Africa and Ukraine". "Thus, the cautious approach by India," one of them said, according to PTI.PM Modi and Trump held bilateral talks on June 17 at Evian-les-Bains on the sidelines of the G7 summit. The meeting was seen as an effort to stabilise ties between India and the US after relations had come under strain over the preceding year.The clarification came after US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor said that New Delhi had informed the American side ahead of the meeting that it preferred not to have questions from the media.Gor, speaking at the Economic Times World Leaders Forum on Sunday, had said India wanted media access without a full-fledged press conference. He recalled discussing the matter with Trump before the meeting."We were behind the scenes, behind the stage, and at one point it was just the president and I, and he asked me, he goes, âWhat the Indians are going to raise?â We went over some topics," Gor said."And he (Trump) said, âDo they have any asks?â And the MEA had one ask. He said, and it was, âLetâs bring in the media, but letâs not do a full press conference,â" the ambassador added.Gor said he conveyed the preference to Trump. "I told the president, I said, the Indians prefer no questions. He said, 'Sure, no problem'," he recalled.During the meeting on June 17, Trump also praised PM Modi, saying India would continue to play a major role globally as long as he remained in office. Asked about India's role in West Asia, Trump said: âYes, I do. I think India plays a big role in everything. As long as he (PM Narendra Modi) is the leader, India is going to play a big role.âTrump also praised PM Modi personally, saying: "So you look at this man. I'll give you a lesson. He's the most beautiful-looking man. He looks so nice. He's like an angel. But actually, he's tough, he's a killer. He's as tough as they come. But he looks so good. So he gets you by surprise," the POTUS said.He added that the US would help India if it came under attack: "If they (India) are attacked and he's (PM Modi) the leader, we would be there to help," Trump said.

World.title: Govt seeks generation data from rooftop solar
World.content:
NEW DELHI: As the number of households installing rooftop solar (RTS) systems under the PM Surya Ghar scheme rises and renewable energy capacity increases, govt has decided to track how much electricity these systems are actually generating, with inverter makers required to share daily generation data with the national portal.

The move could give govt, for the first time, a system to monitor the performance of individual RTS installations rather than merely track the capacity added under the scheme.

Under new guidelines issued by the ministry of new and renewable energy, inverter manufacturers will have to provide daily cumulative generation data through an API to the national portal, mapped to the deviceâs serial number. The guidelines also require applications, monitoring and control servers and cloud-hosted data linked to inverter systems to be located in India.

The data could help govt assess how much electricity rooftop systems are actually generating and identify under-performing installations. It could also allow generation to be analysed across states and power distribution companies (discoms), providing a clearer picture of the energy benefits being delivered by the scheme.

A govt-appointed Expert Committee on Energy Statistics also flagged the absence of comprehensive data on electricity generated and consumed by decentralised renewable energy systems in a recent report.





Currently, more than 44 lakh RTS systems have been installed under the PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana (PMSGMBY), benefiting over 52 lakh households and adding 15.6 GW of solar capacity.

The committee noted that electricity generated by rooftop solar systems is often consumed at the premises and does not pass through the grid, leaving it outside conventional electricity supply statistics. It said generation, export and self-consumption data from rooftop systems are not uniformly recorded or aggregated by discoms and recommended mandatory collection and reporting of such data to improve the accuracy of Indiaâs electricity statistics.

âElectricity generated from many of these systems is already metered. However, these meter readings are either not visible to the discoms or, even if they are visible, the readings are not recorded systematically and reported,â the committee said.

Alekhya Datta, director, electricity and renewables division, TERI, said national-level centralised monitoring of electricity generation from rooftop solar systems would have multiple benefits.

âIf electricity distribution companies have data on electricity generated by rooftop solar plants (behind the meter) in their respective areas and the units consumed by consumers, they will be able to plan their power purchases accordingly,â Datta said.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

âThe amount of electricity generated by RTS plants will also give an indication of the quality of the system, and this attribute can be used in a vendor rating system as well as help improve operations and maintenance.

Consumers, too, will get a sense of satisfaction from knowing their contribution to the environment.â

Though the ministry has asked all inverter companies to share daily generation data, Datta said only around 15 per cent of inverters currently have the capability to share it through APIs. The govt is also yet to create an integrated dashboard where the data can be collated.

World.title: Surprise protests, GenZ outreach: Rahul Gandhi's new playbook after CJP's success
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

"I will not leave till you lodge an FIR. He has pellet injuries on his body, has lost his eye, and we are demanding an FIR for thisâ¦ I will go outside and sit there until you lodge an FIR.

I will sit for 10 days, 20 days, 30 days, 50 days, six months.

Your government will have a problem."

There is a visible change in how

pushes through issues now. The leader of the opposition in Lok Sabha has a new weapon in his political arsenal: impromptu protests.

For the second time in a month, the Congress leader caught the authorities and, to some extent, even his own party, off guard by taking to the streets of the national capital without prior warning.

When Rahul reached the DCP office in Delhi on August 21 demanding an FIR for Sahil Lochab, who sustained pellet injuries during the July 20 student protest, it was Act 2 of his new playbook of street protest politics.

When the cops dilly-dallied, Rahul refused to budge and staged a sit-in protest outside the police station. Priyanka Gandhi Vadra joined him. Congress leaders began arriving. Rapid Action Force personnel were deployed outside.





A visit to a police office turned into a high-voltage political stand-off and, after six hours of dharna, Delhi Police registered an FIR over the pellet firing.

'Politics of anarchy'

The BJP reacted sharply, calling Rahul's sit-in the 'politics of anarchy'. It argued that an FIR relating to the wider July 20 incident already existed, an investigation was under way and the Congress leader was turning police procedure into a political spectacle.

For Lochab, however, there was a sense of relief. His family had been trying to get his complaint registered since August 14, shuttling between police stations. The 19-year-old, who underwent surgery after pellets struck his right eye, finally had an FIR registered after Rahulâs intervention.

According to Lochab's lawyer, the police returned the complaint after reading it and made them wait for a long time.

For years, opponents have labelled Rahul Gandhi a 'part-time politician' who would raise an issue and then disappear. But this incident reinforced something that has changed about Rahulâs tactics over the past year.

He is no longer content merely to raise an issue. He increasingly wants to enter it, stay with it and, if necessary, physically occupy the space.

Rahul's new playbook

The first display of this surprise street-politics instinct had come a month earlier during the NEET student protests.

On July 21, a day after police used force to stop thousands of students attempting a 'Sansad Chalo' march over exam irregularities, Rahul suddenly headed towards Prime Minister Narendra Modiâs residence and staged a sit-in.

Police had reportedly made arrangements anticipating a Congress protest at Vijay Chowk. Rahul went to Lok Kalyan Marg instead. The move caught security officials by surprise. Rahul, Priyanka and several other opposition leaders were later detained. The visual that immediately took over the news was hard to ignore: the leader of opposition physically struggling with police officers, being dragged away and getting a nosebleed in the chaos.

Police personnel detained Rahul Gandhi during a sit-in protest near the Prime Minister's residence.

That was Act 1.

It came at a time when the Congress was desperately trying to make its presence felt, with Abhijeet Dipkeâs Cockroach Janata Party and climate activist

already leading a massive student protest against the NEET paper leak.

Congress had initially kept its distance, preferring to run its own youth outreach campaign, 'Chhatron Ki Goonj'. But people asked a simple question: If Congress claimed to support student issues, why was it missing from the biggest student movement in Delhi?

When the July 20 Jantar Mantar protest took place and massive outrage erupted over police action against the student protesters, Rahul's approach changed.

The very next day, he moved to the front lines. He stood outside the Prime Minister's house, Congress leaders visited injured students, and police action became a major national debate. Rahul took the issue to Parliament and continued raising the pitch over injuries suffered by students.

And when the larger protest began to recede from the headlines, Rahul stayed with one part of it: the use of pellet guns. He has affirmed that his party will keep raising the issue and demand accountability.

Rahul's changing style

The first major image makeover was when Rahul Gandhi embarked on the '

' from Kanyakumari to Kashmir in 2022. Sceptics and rivals wondered if he would complete the journey. By the time he reached Kashmir months later, after walking thousands of kilometres in his now-signature white T-shirt, one charge had become considerably harder to make: that Rahul was unwilling to put in the physical grind that it takes in politics.

The yatra, on its own, did not help the Congress much. What it did was change the way Rahul himself was seen as a politician.

For months, people saw him walking with the common public rather than delivering a scripted speech from a podium. He met farmers, labourers and students, stopped for conversations, entered homes and sat and ate with people.

The yatra experience also laid the foundation for his growing social media popularity.

His online presence today increasingly relies on short, conversational exchanges that can easily travel as reels and clips.

The second shift came in 2024, when he became the leader of the opposition.

Since then, we have seen a more combative Rahul Gandhi. Whether one agrees with his politics or the issues he raises, he appears considerably more comfortable with confrontation than he once did.

Congress's protests in the Parliament complex have also become more visual and experimental under Rahul.

He repeatedly joined opposition MPs at Makar Dwar over the Election Commissionâs SIR exercise in Bihar, with MPs carrying 'vote chori' placards and demanding its rollback. The protest later moved beyond the Parliament gates, with Rahul and other opposition leaders marching towards the Election Commission before being stopped and detained.

Rahul provokes ministers across the aisle and stays for the response.

He takes an argument from the street into Parliament and, increasingly, carries it back outside again. This is also a part of his renewed Gen Z outreach.

'Chhatron Ki Goonj'

If Bharat Jodo helped Rahul Gandhi build the image of a politician who was more approachable and willing to listen, 'Chhatron Ki Goonj' took that idea to a more specific audience: Gen Z.

The programme began in Kota, where students spoke about paper leaks, recruitment delays, coaching pressure and the uncertainty around exams and jobs.

The format was less rally and more conversation, with Rahul asking questions, listening, and allowing individual experiences to shape the message. That made the outreach more relatable.

His latest Pune edition further widened that outreach by putting young women at the centre of the conversation.

Rahul's call to 'smash the patriarchy' in a stadium full of women was a strong message that came with its own set of criticism.

He spoke about different social expectations for boys and girls, cited the 'Manusmriti' while attacking the BJP-RSS worldview, and told women that they 'belong' to themselves rather than to fathers, husbands or sons, triggering huge applause from the crowd.

While a large section of people lauded the focus on women, the ruling BJP immediately trained its guns on him and asked him to induct women ministers into the Karnataka cabinet, where Congress is in power.

The Jharkhand dilemma

Even as Rahul attacked the BJP over issues such as NEET and paper leaks, major student protests broke out in Jharkhand, where the Congress shares power in the Hemant Soren government. Soon after the Jantar Mantar agitation ended, aspirants took to the streets in Ranchi over alleged irregularities and paper leaks in JPSC and JSSC examinations.

The BJP MP dared Rahul Gandhi to take a decisive political stand instead of limiting his activism to social media platforms.

This time, the criticism was closer to home. Protesters targeted not just chief minister Hemant Soren but Rahul as well, pointing to the irony of him speaking for students nationally while Congress was part of the ruling alliance in Jharkhand.

Effigies of both leaders were burnt, and Rahul was accused of not speaking about Jharkhand issues.

Eventually, Rahul was forced to react and intervene. He asserted that Congress supported students protesting peacefully and said that dialogue was the only way forward.

Rahul Gandhi urged Jharkhand CM Hemant Soren to personally meet representatives of students protesting irregularities in state recruitment examinations and address their remaining concerns.

Rahul wrote an open letter to Soren, requesting the CM to personally meet the students and hear out their grievances. The Jharkhand government later accepted the students' demands.

The episode helped Rahul avoid the charge of being selective on student issues, but it also showed the challenge of claiming an issue as your own: once you do that, you can be questioned even when the government under fire is run by an ally.

Has Rahul evolved as a leader?

For years, Rahul Gandhi was accused of being an inconsistent politician who would raise important issues and then disappear from the conversation. Rivals branded him as an âentitled leaderâ and took âPappuâ digs at him.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

But the old image of Rahul as a reluctant politician is certainly harder to sustain today. From Bharat Jodo to 'Chhatron Ki Goonj', fiery parliamentary confrontations and surprise dharnas, he appears more comfortable playing on the front foot.

However, his latest round of street protests seems to stem from the crisis that the opposition in general and Congress in particular faced as Abhijeet Dipke-led CJP mobilised youth in large numbers and forced the government to make Dharmendra Pradhan resign as Union education minister.

Rahul has made his presence felt, but we will have to wait and see if his new politics translates into electoral success for the Congress.

World.title: Kejriwal to address town hall on E20 petrol policy during Goa visit
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) leader Arvind Kejriwal will address a town hall on E20 petrol policy during his two-day visit to Goa beginning Monday.

Kejriwal landed at Dabolim Airport in south Goa on Sunday, where he was received by local party leaders.

AAP sources said Kejriwal would address a press conference on Monday in Panaji and a town hall a day later on E20 petrol policy.

The AAP, which has two MLAs in the 40-member Goa assembly, has announced a campaign against the "forced implementation" of E20 (ethanol-blended) fuel in the coastal state, which will go to polls in 2027.

Earlier this month, Kejriwal had demanded the government give the option to choose between pure petrol and E20 at fuel pumps.

The Centre introduced E20, a blend of 20 per cent ethanol and 80 per cent petrol, as part of efforts to reduce vehicular emissions and cut dependence on crude oil imports. After a phased rollout, E20 became the only petrol variant available at fuel pumps across the country from April 2026.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The move has triggered concerns among some vehicle owners, with motorists reporting reduced engine performance and apprehensions about damage to fuel lines and other components.





Owners of older vehicles, many of which may not have been designed for high ethanol blends, have been seeking availability of lower blends such as E10.

Industry executives had sought to allay concerns over the use of E20 petrol, saying the fuel has undergone rigorous scientific testing, is safe for both new and older vehicles, and is critical for reducing India's dependence on imported crude oil.

World.title: Karnataka suspends food licences of Amazon, Swiggy Instamart, BigBasket over Datura sale
World.content:
The Karnataka Food Safety and Drug Administration Department has suspended the food licences of Amazon, Swiggy Instamart, and BigBasket until further orders after toxic Datura fruits and seeds were found being sold online as food products.

According to an order issued by Food Safety Commissioner K. Srinivas, the department has also directed the three platforms to immediately remove listings and s for Datura, also known as Dhatura, and stop selling or distributing the products for human consumption.

The action followed inspections by food safety officials, who found Datura fruits and seeds being stored and offered for sale through e-commerce platforms using Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) registration or licence numbers.

Officials said Datura is poisonous and that its sale or distribution as a food product poses a serious public health risk.

Warehouses

During inspections, officials found packets of Datura fruits and seeds carrying food registration numbers. The products were also found stored in a warehouse and listed for sale or distribution through online platforms.

The department said that collecting, selling or distributing Datura fruits or seeds as food was unlawful given their poisonous nature. The action has been initiated under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, and the Food Safety and Standards Rules, 2011.

Explanation sought

Representatives of the three companies appeared before the adjudicating authority on Monday, according to the Commissioner’s order.

Amazon did not submit a response to the notice, while Swiggy Instamart sought more time to submit documents detailing the action it had taken after receiving the department’s notice.

BigBasket told the authority that it had stopped selling Datura and changed the manner in which the product would be sold. It also said that the labelling would be changed to clearly state that the product was “not for human consumption”.

The department, however, found the responses unsatisfactory, citing the poisonous nature of Datura and the potential risk to public health.

Suppliers

The action has also been extended to suppliers and sellers who provided Datura products to the e-commerce platforms.

Food safety authorities have ordered the suspension of their food licences and registrations under the applicable food safety laws. The department has also directed the relevant State or Central licensing authorities to initiate action to cancel the registrations of the organisations or vendors concerned, subject to due legal process.

The department said separate orders would be issued after compliance reports are received and the parties concerned are given an opportunity to present their arguments.

The platforms and food businesses have been directed not to sell, distribute, advertise or display Datura fruits or seeds as food or for human consumption in future. Failure to comply could invite further action under the applicable laws.

World.title: Delhi HC seeks rationalefor MP/MLA endorsementto get Lakshmi Yojana aid
World.content:
The Delhi High Court on Monday asked the Delhi government to file an affidavit within 10 days explaining why women seeking financial assistance under the Delhi Lakshmi Yojana must obtain an endorsement from their MP or MLA.

A Bench of Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia questioned the rationale for making endorsement from an elected representative mandatory for every applicant to the scheme, which provides financial assistance of ₹2,500 a month.

The court sought the government’s response while hearing a plea by former Congress councillor Abhishek Dutt and Aya Nagar councillor Vedpal Sheetal Chaudhary, challenging the provision and arguing that it gives political representatives “unbridled discretion” and effectively turns a welfare entitlement into an “instrument of political patronage”.

“Let a short affidavit be filed by respondent No. 1 (Delhi government)... and indicate what objective they are seeking to achieve by adding this clause in the scheme,” stated the Bench.

Additional Solicitor General Chetan Sharma, appearing for the Delhi government, defended the provision, submitting that similar schemes operated in other States and that such requirements exist across the country.

The matter will be heard next on October 17.

The scheme became operational on August 1 with the launch of an online registration portal. Under the scheme, women aged 21 to 60 with an annual family income of up to ₹2.5 lakh are eligible to apply. Income-tax payers and government employees are excluded. Families with more than three children, ownership of a four-wheeler or a member in government service are not eligible.

World.title: Cong. protests FIRs against IYC workers in Gurugram
World.content:
Led by Haryana Pradesh Congress Committee (HPCC) president Rao Narender Singh, party leaders and workers staged a demonstration in Gurugram against the FIRs registered against Indian Youth Congress (IYC) and NSUI workers and student leaders for allegedly waving black flags at Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini during his visit to the city on August 21.

Later, party leaders submitted a memorandum to the Gurugram Police Commissioner, demanding immediate, impartial and transparent action in the matter.

Mr. Singh demanded withdrawal of the FIRs registered against Youth Congress and NSUI workers, as well as the district presidents of Gurugram Rural and Gurugram Urban. He also called for an immediate end to the alleged harassment and intimidation of Congress workers and their families.

He also demanded independent medical examinations of youth workers, student leaders and district presidents who have alleged assault or harassment while in police custody. He also sought preservation of CCTV footage from the relevant locations and legal and departmental action against police personnel found responsible for any wrongdoing.

Mr. Singh said right to peacefully protest and express one’s views was fundamental to a democracy. He warned that the alleged misuse of police machinery to suppress political dissent would not be tolerated. “Our youth workers, students and district presidents are the voice of democracy. Every attempt to silence that voice will be answered democratically,” he said.

Gurugram Police had arrested eight Congress workers on charges related to obstructing VIP security arrangements, disrupting government duty and attempting to stop the Chief Minister’s convoy while displaying black flags. The protest was reportedly linked to concerns over infrastructure at Gurugram University.

Following the incident, show-cause notices were issued to the Deputy Commissioners of Police (West) and Crime, fixing responsibility for the episode. Orders were also issued to suspend the Station House Officer of Civil Lines Police Station and several police personnel deployed with him. A departmental inquiry was additionally ordered against the Intelligence In-charge.

World.title: Stalin moves Madras High Court to declare him elected from Kolathur constituency
World.content:
DMK president M.K. Stalin has filed a writ petition in the Madras High Court, seeking 100% counting of VVPAT slips of the Kolathur Assembly constituency, and consequently to declare him as the returned candidate after nullifying the election of TVK MLA V.S. Babu.

Though Article 329(b) of the Constitution states that no election to Parliament or a State legislature could be called into question except by way of an election petition, the petitioner said his writ petition would be maintainable since he was only challenging the post-result administrative/technical process of EVM/VVPAT checking and verification.

Mr. Stalin said the Supreme Court had, in its 2024 judgment in Association for Democratic Reforms versus Election Commission of India, permitted either the runner-up or the third place holder in a parliamentary/Assembly election to make a request for checking and verification of the burnt memory/microcontroller in 5% of the EVMs by a team of engineers from the EVM manufacturers.

In the 2026 Assembly polls, the petitioner stood second, securing 74,202 votes, and was declared to have lost to Mr. Babu, who had secured 82,997 votes. Hence, he made an application on May 7 for verifying 14 (5%) of the 286 EVM sets used in the Kolathur constituency.

Though the application was made within three days of the declaration of the election results on May 4, the verification process began only on July 29. “This inordinate delay (of nearly three months) is itself contrary to the spirit of the directions issued by the honourable Supreme Court, and has caused serious and irreversible prejudice to my legal rights,” the petitioner said.

Informing the court that he had appointed senior counsel N.R. Elango as his representative for the verification process, Mr. Stalin said one of the VVPAT units had stopped working during the mock poll and began displaying an error on July 30. He complained that another VVPAT unit also stopped working during the verification process that continued on July 31.

The petitioner said his representative was not furnished with any report either from an engineer of Bharat Electronics Limited or any other competent authority explaining the cause of the failure of the two VVPAT units. On the other hand, the petitioner’s representative was only given the option to choose an EVM from any other polling station for verification.

In one of the EVMs taken up for verification, the address tags on the carrying cases on the ballot unit and control unit were found to be new and unfilled. Further, the seal on those address tags were found affixed on the reverse side, contrary to the practice observed in respect of every other EVM set on which the seal was affixed on the front.

Stating that Mr. Elango had on August 4 requested election officials for verification of EVM sets from six additional polling stations, the petitioner added that on August 5, another “alarming irregularity” came to light when one of the ballot units bearing his name was unable to detect the control unit.

Without addressing the serious lapses, the District Election Officer passed an order on August 5, declaring that the verification process had been concluded successfully, he said.

Another writ petition

Mr. Stalin has also filed another writ petition challenging the constitutional validity of certain provisions of the Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) formulated by the ECI for checking and verification of the burnt memory/microcontroller in 5% of the EVMs as per the Supreme Court directives. He has urged the court to declare as unconstitutional paragraphs 4(a) and 4(c) of the Administrative SOP and paragraph 4.2(p) of the Technical SOP.

World.title: IIT Delhi students protest after student death, allege institutional negligence
World.content:
Students at the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Delhi on Monday boycotted classes and staged a protest demanding an independent investigation into the alleged suicide of a 31-year-old MSc student, two days after his death on campus.

The protesting students alleged that “administrative lapses” had led to the student’s death and demanded that the institute suspend classes at the Lecture Hall Complex (LHC), where his body was found.

“Students should not be made to go back to the LHC thinking it is business as usual. The system needs to take a pause,” the students wrote in a note submitted to IIT Delhi Director Rangan Banerjee on Monday.

Speaking on condition of anonymity, a student alleged that the administration had been portraying the deceased as mentally unwell instead of taking responsibility.

“The administration has been telling us that he was mentally unwell and that the psychiatrists could not do anything to help him, instead of taking accountability. He had been referred to VIMHANS for treatment, after which he was not allocated his hostel room back. He was staying off campus, and this put him under a lot of financial distress,” the student said.

Major academic issues

In the note, the students demanded that the competent authority explain how issues such as the non-allocation of hostel accommodation, the denial of academic projects and an unsupportive hospital administration within a highly competitive academic environment could cause or exacerbate mental distress among students.

The students also demanded the resignation of two administrative officials over what they described as “negligence and insensitive comments”.

The students sought clear communication from the authorities on measures taken to address mental health on campus, adding: “In the last 30 months, eight IIT Delhi students died by suicide on campus. This pattern points to a systemic problem.”

The students added that classes were called off by midday as they gathered at the LHC, and also demanded that no action be taken against those participating in the protest.

On Saturday night, the institute expressed its condolences over the student’s death and said the police were investigating the incident.

When contacted, IIT Delhi officials did not respond to The Hindu’s queries about the protest, the allegations or the students’ demands.
